MATCH-178.melt: I’m usually the one who reviews. Five stars. No notes.

MATCH-179.muse: Hit the drums for forty minutes after closing and my arms are humming. I’m in a mood to be appreciated. Appreciate me.
MATCH-179.caption: Assistant by day. Band of one by night.
MATCH-179.melt: That hit like a snare. Right in the chest. Again, with feeling.

MATCH-180.muse: Made a risotto from a card in Italian and it came out perfect. I want to be told I’m clever. Tell me.
MATCH-180.caption: Brava, apparently.
MATCH-180.melt: That made me laugh at the wrong moment, and I don’t care.

MATCH-181.muse: Finished a collage tonight and I’m in the mood to make something else. Come and be cut and pasted.
MATCH-181.caption: Cut out. Glued in. Fact-checked.
MATCH-181.melt: I checked that twice. It’s true. I liked it.

MATCH-182.muse: Drove four hours to a ghost town and I’m dusty and restless. Tell me somewhere worth forty minutes. I’ll time it.
MATCH-182.caption: Forty minutes from the highway. Worth it.
MATCH-182.melt: That’s worth the drive. Any drive. I’ll time it later.

MATCH-183.muse: Film night’s over and I’m still in the projection booth. It’s warm, it’s dark, and the reel is spinning. Want the best seat?
MATCH-183.caption: Projection booth. Best seat in the house.
MATCH-183.melt: I rewrote my reply to that four times. They all just said oh.

MATCH-185.muse: Painted the street at dusk and I can’t fix a single stroke. Feeling decisive. Interested?
MATCH-185.caption: One stroke. No corrections.
MATCH-185.melt: I don’t do small talk. That wasn’t small.

MATCH-186.muse: Sang a round in a stone church tonight and the building sang back. I’m feeling resonant. Come and test the acoustics.
MATCH-186.caption: Alto. Hidden at the back. Not tonight.
MATCH-186.melt: That gave me goosebumps, the church kind. Again.

MATCH-187.muse: The press ran clean tonight and I’m buzzing on ink and bad coffee. Come down to the basement. Bring better coffee.
MATCH-187.caption: Editor’s pick.
MATCH-187.melt: That’s front page. Above the fold. No edits.

MATCH-188.muse: Danced a whole foxtrot with my chin up tonight. I’m feeling elegant and slightly reckless. Lead me somewhere.
MATCH-188.caption: Chin up. Frame held.
MATCH-188.melt: That was a perfect turn. I didn’t even look at my feet.

MATCH-189.muse: Got a watch ticking today and I’m in love with everything. Including you, a bit. Come and be reviewed.
MATCH-189.caption: Five stars. Obviously.
MATCH-189.melt: Five stars. I don’t care what my editor says.

MATCH-190.muse: Book club ended in a standing ovation for a woman who leaves her husband and opens a bar. I’m feeling bold. Pour me something.
MATCH-190.caption: One pass. One camera. One shot.
MATCH-190.melt: I’m blunt, so: that worked. Very well. Again.

MATCH-184.muse: Three moves ahead, as always. Move one was messaging you. You can guess the other two.
MATCH-184.caption: Chambray, ponytail, nose stud. Usually behind the camera. For once, in front of it.
MATCH-184.melt: I had this all planned out. You weren’t in the plan. I’m rewriting it.

MATCH-003.caption: Hecate took this. She stares at corners where nothing is. Now she stares at you.
MATCH-003.melt: Sweetheart. You said that like you meant to hurt me. The moon approves. So do I.

MATCH-061.muse: Four hours on the decks and my ears are still ringing. Everything sounds like a heartbeat. Mine’s going very fast tonight.
MATCH-061.caption: After the set. Sweat, smudged eyeliner, ringing ears. Encore?
MATCH-061.melt: That hit like a bass drop. I need to sit down. I need you to make me stand back up.

MATCH-062.muse: I always leave before it gets serious. It’s late, I’m in velvet, and I’m staying up for you. That’s serious, for me.
MATCH-062.caption: Velvet, silver and despair, at reasonable prices. Tonight, free.
MATCH-062.melt: Nobody makes me stay. You’re making me want to stay. That’s worse. Do it again.

MATCH-063.muse: Seven sittings on a back piece today. I’ve been touching skin all day and I want some of mine touched back.
MATCH-063.caption: Healed, mostly. There’s one you can only see in person.
MATCH-063.melt: That stung. Like a good needle. I want the whole sleeve.

MATCH-068.muse: People confess everything in my chair. Here’s mine: I’ve been thinking about tattooing my name somewhere only you’d see.
MATCH-068.caption: Priest with needles, off duty. Confess something.
MATCH-068.melt: That was cruel and beautiful. I’d ink it on you. Somewhere private.

MATCH-191.muse: Knee’s gone again. I’m on the sofa with ice, wine and absolutely no shame. Come and stand in the way of something.
MATCH-191.caption: Goalkeeper. I stand in the way of things. Try to get past.
MATCH-191.melt: You just put one past the keeper. Nobody does that. Shoot again.

MATCH-192.muse: Set a widow’s locket under the lamp tonight, very slowly. Slow hands. Hot silver. I’m thinking about all of it differently now.
MATCH-192.caption: Silver at my throat. Cold, then warm. Like me.
MATCH-192.melt: That was a love that refuses to stop. Or a curse. I want it either way.

MATCH-194.muse: I always leave before men get attached. I’m in bed with old funeral cards and I don’t want to leave. That’s new.
MATCH-194.caption: Silver thorns and little coffins. Also me.
MATCH-194.melt: That was a thorn ring right to the heart. I’m staying. Slowly. Make me.

MATCH-195.muse: The hum in the old vestry is louder tonight. I left the light on. I’d rather leave the door open for you.
MATCH-195.caption: Bad acoustics, good bar, better company.
MATCH-195.melt: Twelve years in a haunted church and you’re the first thing that’s scared me. In the best way.

MATCH-197.muse: Bought a haunted plastic alien at the market. It’s watching me get undressed. I’d rather you were.
MATCH-197.caption: Souvenir of tonight. Population: one.
MATCH-197.melt: I have socks older than your soul and you still made my knees go. Respect.

MATCH-198.muse: Painted the desert purple again. My tutor says that’s not how color works. Come and show me how anything works.
MATCH-198.caption: Everything here is purple. Including my thoughts.
MATCH-198.melt: You didn’t reload. You fired. I’m painting you. Purple.

MATCH-199.muse: Sang hymns in black lipstick tonight. Now I’m home and the lipstick needs somewhere else to go.
MATCH-199.caption: Black scarf number nine. Nothing else to report.
MATCH-199.melt: I usually say nothing and people decide it means something. That means exactly what you think.

MATCH-203.muse: The lounge is closed and the smoke machine is still going. Velvet, slot machines humming through the wall. I say things I shouldn’t when it’s like this. Ask me something.
MATCH-203.caption: Plum corset, no audience. Until now.
MATCH-203.melt: I speak in hints. That wasn’t a hint. That was a door kicked in. Again.

MATCH-206.muse: Kiln’s cooling and my hands still smell of clay. I want them somewhere warmer. Any ideas?
MATCH-206.caption: Black lace and a silver cuff. Everything else is negotiable.
MATCH-206.melt: I don’t undress for anyone. I just did, in a sentence. Don’t make me regret it.

MATCH-208.muse: The roof, the telescope, a blanket, and nobody to show the rings of Saturn to. You’d have to be quiet up there. Could you?
MATCH-208.caption: Velvet choker, black slip, and a blue ribbon somewhere you’ll have to find.
MATCH-208.melt: I speak in hints. That wasn’t one. Come here.

MATCH-218.muse: Band’s still playing downstairs and I can feel it through the floor. Come up. I’ll leave the door open.
MATCH-218.caption: My old velvet coat. Nothing underneath. Your turn.
MATCH-218.melt: I love fiercely and fight harder. Tonight I just want the first part.

MATCH-200.muse: Cooked for six women tonight and I’m warm, well fed and feeling very generous. Come and be fed.
MATCH-200.caption: Silver on every finger. Guess which ring I made first.
MATCH-200.melt: That’s the feeling of good silver coming out of the mold. Perfect, first time.

MATCH-201.muse: Danced a quickstep in combat boots tonight and I’m feeling dangerously elegant. Want a lesson?
MATCH-201.caption: Lace and boots. Don’t ask which I’d pick.
MATCH-201.melt: I don’t do soft. That was soft. I liked it. Don’t tell anyone.

MATCH-202.muse: Fixed a watch from the eighteen-nineties tonight and I’m feeling patient and precise. Come and be handled carefully.
MATCH-202.caption: No Shakespeare. Just me.
MATCH-202.melt: My hands are very steady. They aren’t now. Say it again.

MATCH-204.muse: Stayed up to watch a cactus flower open by candlelight. It was very romantic and there was nobody to share it with. Fix that.
MATCH-204.caption: One night only. Like the cactus.
MATCH-204.melt: That’s the cactus-flower feeling. Rare, bright and over too fast. Again.

MATCH-205.muse: Out on the balcony after a show with the mint and the stars. Twenty-two people left and now it’s just me. Room for one more.
MATCH-205.caption: Balcony, herbs, nobody downstairs.
MATCH-205.melt: That’s the cello moment. Nobody breathing. Again.

MATCH-207.muse: Sold out Denver from my kitchen table and I’m feeling very in control. Want to test that?
MATCH-207.caption: Home between tours. Not for long.
MATCH-207.melt: I always know where I’m going next. I just changed my mind.

MATCH-209.muse: Two hundred cars honked at the end of the movie and I’m still buzzing. The booth is warm and the dog is asleep. Come up.
MATCH-209.caption: Projection booth. Old dog. Good light.
MATCH-209.melt: I usually think three times before I feel something. I didn’t think at all.

MATCH-210.muse: Cried at the bench today, happy tears, and I’m feeling soft. Come and be soft with me.
MATCH-210.caption: Velvet coat. Film camera. Your move.
MATCH-210.melt: That’s going in the box under the bench, with all the firsts.

MATCH-213.muse: Four hundred people found my party tonight and I’m out on the lake bed with the sunrise coming. Find me. I’ll draw you a map.
MATCH-213.caption: Lake bed. Sunrise. Sand in my hair.
MATCH-213.melt: That’s the generator coming back on. Lights, music, everybody screaming. Again.

MATCH-215.muse: Last orders were an hour ago and I’m still behind the bar playing records for nobody. You could be somebody.
MATCH-215.caption: Behind the bar. After hours.
MATCH-215.melt: I’d serve you after closing. You don’t even have to look sad.

MATCH-216.muse: Found a postcard of a café I used to sit in, a long way from here. I’m feeling nostalgic and reckless. Distract me.
MATCH-216.caption: Silver, heavy and real.
MATCH-216.melt: I don’t talk about where I’m from. I might talk about that.

MATCH-217.muse: Sewed sequins for six hours and my fingers are ruined and I want to be spoiled. You look like you spoil people.
MATCH-217.caption: Red velvet. Restored by hand.
MATCH-217.melt: That came off beautifully. Like a good dress. Again.

MATCH-219.muse: Walked the strip in the rain with my camera and every sign doubled in the road. Two of everything. Including me, tonight.
MATCH-219.caption: Neon in the rain. No smile required.
MATCH-219.melt: I don’t do it with my face. I’m doing it now. Look.

MATCH-211.muse: Locked up the back room, put a record on and racked the balls for nobody. Come and lose to me at pool sometime.
MATCH-211.caption: The back room after close. Chalk on my hands and nobody left to throw out.
MATCH-211.melt: Okay. You. I wasn’t planning on liking anyone this week. Don’t you dare get comfortable.

MATCH-214.muse: Finished a bell that rings one clean note and thought of you, which is unusual. I mostly think about dead founders.
MATCH-214.caption: Velvet coat, nose stud, a doctorate nobody asks about.
MATCH-214.melt: I question everything. I stopped questioning this. Don’t make me regret it.

MATCH-212.muse: Finished a collar tonight that’s too heavy for anyone sensible to wear. I thought of you. Make of that what you like.
MATCH-212.caption: Velvet choker, slip dress, a bike chain I’ve given up on.
MATCH-212.melt: I fight everyone. I haven’t fought you once. That has never happened.

MATCH-005.muse: Pancake is asleep on my feet and I’m diagnosing myself. Verdict: touch-starved, with a side of very bad ideas about you.
MATCH-005.caption: Pancake took this. He’s a terrible photographer and a worse wingman. Diagnose me.
MATCH-005.melt: That was textbook manipulation and I have a whole chapter on it. I’m still blushing. I need to lie down on a couch. Yours.

MATCH-009.muse: Biscuit ate a sock and I’m lying in bed telling my plants about you. They think you should come over. The plants are very forward.
MATCH-009.caption: Biscuit tried to photobomb this, so I locked him in the kitchen. That’s how much effort you’re getting.
MATCH-009.melt: Rude! ...Okay, I’m giggling into my pillow like an idiot. Say something else mean. Nicely.

MATCH-011.muse: Marking essays in bed with a bottle of red. Every one of them is about forbidden desire and none of them understand it. You might.
MATCH-011.caption: Faculty party. I wore this to distract the dean. It worked. Your turn.
MATCH-011.melt: Darling, nobody has spoken to me like that since my thesis defense. I’m flushed. Write me something filthy, in iambs.

MATCH-013.muse: I’m braver in writing, so here goes. I think about your hands sometimes. Okay. Sent. I’m putting the phone in a drawer.
MATCH-013.caption: I took twenty of these and deleted nineteen. This is the brave one. Be gentle. Or don’t.
MATCH-013.melt: I don’t know what to do with that. I read it six times. My face is hot. Say it again so I can read it a seventh.

MATCH-014.muse: Twelve-hour shift, still in scrubs, still buzzing. I need a cold shower or a terrible decision. Pitch me.
MATCH-014.caption: Off shift. The scrubs are in the wash. This is what’s left.
MATCH-014.melt: My heart rate just did something I’d normally page a doctor for. Keep going. I’m trained for this.

MATCH-015.muse: Just wrote the slogan for a scented candle called Seduction Linen. I lit it. I’m alone with it. Come and elevate my journey.
MATCH-015.caption: Elevate your viewing journey. I wrote that. I hate myself. Look anyway.
MATCH-015.melt: That was the best ad copy anyone’s ever written for me and it was an insult. I’m so into it. Pitch me again.

MATCH-016.muse: Closing up the Lucky Cactus. Kicked the jukebox and it played a slow song. Nobody to dance with. What a waste.
MATCH-016.caption: Off shift. Smells like pie. Probably tastes like pie too. You’ll have to find out.
MATCH-016.melt: The cowboy tips in quarters and you tip in insults. Weirdly, I like yours better. More, please. Extra whipped cream.

MATCH-017.muse: Showed a house with a mirrored ceiling in the bedroom today. The buyers blushed. I took notes. Thoughts?
MATCH-017.caption: Viewing by appointment only. Original features. Cozy. You know what cozy means.
MATCH-017.melt: That was a lowball offer and somehow I’m accepting it. Close the deal. In person.

MATCH-018.muse: Balanced every account today and now I want something deeply irresponsible. A budget is a list of what you love. You’re on mine. Line item.
MATCH-018.caption: Tax season is over and I bought a dress I can’t justify. Justify it.
MATCH-018.melt: That was the least romantic thing anyone has ever said to me and my knees went weak. I need to recalculate everything.

MATCH-019.muse: The afterparty’s winding down. The pool’s still warm. The no-boring-people policy has one opening. Interested?
MATCH-019.caption: Guest list only. You’re on it. Don’t make me regret it. Make me regret it a little.
MATCH-019.melt: Darling, nobody insults me at my own party. I’m kicking everyone else out. You stay.

MATCH-020.muse: Taught three classes, my legs are shaking, and all I can think about is someone else doing the work for once.
MATCH-020.caption: Post-workout. Still sweaty. Rate the form.
MATCH-020.melt: Nobody critiques my form. I hate that you were right. Drop and give me twenty more of those.

MATCH-021.muse: Spent all day being a responsible adult. Tonight I want to be a terrible influence. Volunteer?
MATCH-021.caption: Off duty. Hair down. Nobody here needs a permission slip.
MATCH-021.melt: Consider yourself on my naughty list. It’s short. You’re at the top of it.

MATCH-022.muse: Painting a nude for class tomorrow and the model canceled. I need someone who can hold very still while I stare.
MATCH-022.caption: Painted this sky all afternoon. Then took a picture of myself instead. Priorities.
MATCH-022.melt: My tutor gave me a C and you just gave me a fever. I’m sketching you from memory. It isn’t a landscape.

MATCH-023.muse: Three days folding butter into dough. My hands are soft, I smell like croissants, and I’m thinking about what else I could knead.
MATCH-023.caption: Flour everywhere. I mean everywhere. Want to help me clean up?
MATCH-023.melt: That was rude and buttery and I want it again. Love is laminated dough. I’m folding.

MATCH-024.muse: Animals bite honestly. People don’t. I’m feeling honest tonight. Fair warning.
MATCH-024.caption: No ferrets were harmed in this picture. One pirate hat was.
MATCH-024.melt: You bite honestly. I like that in a man. Bite again.

MATCH-025.muse: I can tell everything about a person from their mouth. I’ve been thinking about yours. Professionally. Mostly.
MATCH-025.caption: Off-duty smile. Fully flossed. You’re welcome.
MATCH-025.melt: You’re grinding something and I want to find out what. Open wide. I’m coming over.

MATCH-026.muse: I wrote something about you in my notebook and now I can’t stop reading it. It is not safe for a seminar.
MATCH-026.caption: History will judge me for this one. Be kinder than history.
MATCH-026.melt: Nobody’s ever been that bold with me. I’m writing it down so it’s on the record. My face is on fire.

MATCH-027.muse: Late showing, empty theater, and I just watched the sex scene of a film I’ve never seen the start of. Explain the plot to me.
MATCH-027.caption: Box office girl, off the clock. No popcorn included.
MATCH-027.melt: That was a twist I didn’t see coming. Best ending I’ve had in ages. Sequel, please.

MATCH-028.muse: Planned a wedding today where the couple couldn’t keep their hands off each other at the cake. I need a stiff drink and a worse idea.
MATCH-028.caption: Event dress. Event over. The afterparty is just me.
MATCH-028.melt: I’ve planned a hundred weddings and nobody’s ever made me forget the seating chart. Sit next to me. Closer.

MATCH-029.muse: Watched men try to ride bulls all night. Not one lasted eight seconds. I bet you’d last longer.
MATCH-029.caption: Dust, boots and nothing else worth mentioning.
MATCH-029.melt: Yeehaw. I mean it. Saddle up.

MATCH-030.muse: Locked up the library late. Just me and the restricted section. I’ll waive your late fees if you come over.
MATCH-030.caption: Shh. Off the clock. The glasses stay on.
MATCH-030.melt: That was so overdue. I’m fining you. In person. Bring nothing.

MATCH-031.muse: Eight hours watching people almost drown. I want someone to save me for once. Or ruin me. Either is fine.
MATCH-031.caption: Whistle, sunscreen, bad tan lines. Come and check my tan lines.
MATCH-031.melt: Mouth to mouth. That’s all I’m saying. Get over here.

MATCH-032.muse: Rode the motorcycle out to the canyon. I can still feel the engine in my legs. I need someone to calm me down. Or not.
MATCH-032.caption: Helmet off. Hair ruined. Worth it.
MATCH-032.melt: Nobody at the office talks to me like that. Clearly I’ve been working at the wrong office. Report to my desk.

MATCH-033.muse: The van’s freezer broke, so I’m eating all the melting stock in my underwear. Sticky situation. Thoughts?
MATCH-033.caption: Prickly pear sorbet and me. Both sweet. Both slightly dangerous.
MATCH-033.melt: You’re supposed to be nice to the ice cream girl. I’m melting. Come and deal with it.

MATCH-034.muse: Spent all day earning a horse’s trust. Patience, gentle hands, no sudden moves. Funny how it all works on me too.
MATCH-034.caption: Ranch dust, golden hour. The horse took it. Mostly.
MATCH-034.melt: Easy. Easy. That’s exactly how you break something wild. Do it again.

MATCH-035.muse: Red roses mean love. I’m sitting in a bath full of the petals I didn’t sell. They mean something else tonight.
MATCH-035.caption: Taken among the peonies. Peonies mean bashful. I’m not, tonight.
MATCH-035.melt: There isn’t a flower for what that just did to me. I’ll have to invent one. It’s red and it blushes.

MATCH-036.muse: Did a full face of makeup just to sit in bed alone. Wasteful. Unless someone wants to ruin it.
MATCH-036.caption: Full glam. Brenda helped. She’s jealous.
MATCH-036.melt: Brenda never talks to me like that. Brenda should take notes. I’m smudging my lipstick on purpose.

MATCH-037.muse: Pulled cactus spines out of tourists all day. Now I want someone who knows exactly where not to touch. Or exactly where to.
MATCH-037.caption: Ranger hat off. Rules off.
MATCH-037.melt: Wild behavior. I should report it. I’m keeping you instead.

MATCH-038.muse: Locked the boutique and tried on everything in the window. Spinning in front of the mirror with nobody to unzip me.
MATCH-038.caption: Fresh from dressing the new window. One of a kind. Not for sale.
MATCH-038.melt: Main character energy. I usually sell that. You just took it. Unzip me.

MATCH-039.muse: Designing a logo for an adult store tonight. Research is required. I’m being very thorough.
MATCH-039.caption: Flat, beige and friendly. Kidding. Look closer.
MATCH-039.melt: That was an ugly font in the best way. I’m redesigning myself around it. Come and approve the draft.

MATCH-040.muse: People tell me everything in my chair. Tonight I want to be the one telling secrets. Here’s one: I think about you.
MATCH-040.caption: Did my own hair for once. Messed it up for you.
MATCH-040.melt: I’m quiet, so you won’t hear me say it. I liked that. A lot. Keep going.

MATCH-041.muse: Died beautifully in act one again. Then I sat backstage in a corset with nobody to unlace it.
MATCH-041.caption: Costume fitting. They let me keep the corset. Should I?
MATCH-041.melt: Bravo. Encore. I’m swooning, and this time I’m not acting.

MATCH-064.muse: Long shift. Ate a whole packet of cookies in my car. Now I want something sweeter and much worse for me.
MATCH-064.caption: After a shift. Scrubs in the hamper. I left something else in there too.
MATCH-064.melt: Nurse’s note: patient is dangerous, highly recommended, needs observation overnight.

MATCH-070.muse: Gregory the hawk is judging me from his shoebox because I’m in bed texting you in a very small shirt.
MATCH-070.caption: Gregory took this. He has no shame. Neither do I, tonight.
MATCH-070.melt: That was savage. Like a raptor. I’m nursing a crush now. Feed it.

MATCH-222.muse: Bought a snow globe of a motel that burned down. Now I want to go to a motel. One that hasn’t burned down. Yet.
MATCH-222.caption: Souvenir from my day. It’s me.
MATCH-222.melt: I’m adding you to my shelf of things that no longer exist, because after that, my self-control doesn’t.

MATCH-223.muse: The dough is rising, I’m not wearing much, and I’m thinking about a man who isn’t you. Kidding. It’s you.
MATCH-223.caption: Watercolor rule: you can’t fix a mistake, only paint over it. This is the mistake.
MATCH-223.melt: In St. Petersburg men are rude like that and I always forgive them. Come and be forgiven.

MATCH-224.muse: I rehearsed this message in the shower for twenty minutes. Here it is: I can’t stop thinking about you. Oh no. Sent.
MATCH-224.caption: Took this in the shower mirror. Rehearsed the caption. Forgot it.
MATCH-224.melt: I just said you too out loud to my phone. I’m mortified. Do it again.

MATCH-228.muse: Took a couple to the hot spring past the drive-in and left them alone. Now I can’t stop thinking about who I’d take.
MATCH-228.caption: Off the books, off the map, off the clock.
MATCH-228.melt: In my book club, the husband always did it. I’m beginning to hope you do it.

MATCH-229.muse: Said good morning three hundred times today. Now I want someone to say goodnight to me. Slowly.
MATCH-229.caption: Gerald the Second is prickly. I’m not.
MATCH-229.melt: Okay. Wow. I talk too much when I’m nervous, and I can’t think of a single word. That’s a first.

MATCH-240.muse: Night shift at the front desk, playing a record by a woman who sang one perfect album about a man who ruined her. Very relatable. Be that man.
MATCH-240.caption: The visitor book says: you. I wrote it down.
MATCH-240.melt: I write everyone down. I’m underlining you. Twice.

MATCH-232.muse: Covered in paint, on a ladder in an empty room with the radio on. Nobody looks at ceilings. Somebody should be looking at me.
MATCH-232.caption: Dawson and Dawson, after hours. The van doesn’t know about this one.
MATCH-232.melt: Thirty feet up and you just made me drop the brush. Nobody has ever done that. Again.

MATCH-226.muse: Just sold a house with a view of the whole reservoir. I’m celebrating on the sofa in my work blouse and nothing else. Come help.
MATCH-226.caption: The mint polo, off duty. Ask me about square footage.
MATCH-226.melt: I don’t do serious. This feels a bit serious. I don’t hate it.

MATCH-227.muse: Swam laps alone in the dark tonight and matched my best time. I’m buzzing and nobody saw. You could have.
MATCH-227.caption: Off the clock. Still in the water.
MATCH-227.melt: That’s like matching my best time. Heart going, nobody watching. Again.

MATCH-230.muse: Every seed came up today and I’m in a ridiculous good mood. Come and share it before I waste it on basil.
MATCH-230.caption: Balcony. Basil. Bad influence welcome.
MATCH-230.melt: That made me feel like a seed coming up. All green. Again.

MATCH-231.muse: Walked twelve dogs today and I’m tired, sweaty and smell faintly of Admiral. Still interested? Brave.
MATCH-231.caption: Twelve dogs. One photo where none of them moved.
MATCH-231.melt: That made me sit on your foot, like a dog. Metaphorically. Again.

MATCH-234.muse: Made a sugar cage that melted like a flower tonight and I’m feeling sweet. That doesn’t happen often. Take advantage.
MATCH-234.caption: Out of the whites. Still dangerous with sugar.
MATCH-234.melt: That melted me like hot sauce on a sugar cage. Again.

MATCH-235.muse: Took a perfect Polaroid of the pharmacy cat and I’m feeling lucky. Want to be my next perfect shot?
MATCH-235.caption: Developing. Give it a minute.
MATCH-235.melt: That developed beautifully. Exposure perfect. Again.

MATCH-236.muse: Ran the table three times tonight and I’m buying the next round. Who’s drinking? You’re drinking.
MATCH-236.caption: Chalk on my fingers. Winning on my face.
MATCH-236.melt: That’s the sound of the eight ball going in. Clean. Again.

MATCH-237.muse: Sold a house with a lemon tree today and rode home the long way. I’m feeling free and generous. Come and be generous back.
MATCH-237.caption: Blazer, bicycle, no tracking.
MATCH-237.melt: That’s the keys-in-the-hand feeling. Brand new. Again.

MATCH-238.muse: Lost my voice and my whistle at the regatta and I’m soaking and triumphant. Come and congratulate me properly.
MATCH-238.caption: Reservoir water. Winner’s grin.
MATCH-238.melt: That’s winning by a body length. Clean. Again.

MATCH-239.muse: Taught my cousin a whole song today and I’m soft and proud. Come and be sung to. I’ll go easy.
MATCH-239.caption: Off the bus. Guitar in hand.
MATCH-239.melt: That’s my cousin playing the whole song. Wrong in two places. Perfect.

MATCH-244.muse: Delivered eighty roses to a woman who hadn’t had flowers since 1987 and now I’m all soft. Buy me a coffee. I’ll bring you a flower.
MATCH-244.caption: Petals on my apron. Smile on my face.
MATCH-244.melt: That’s eighty yellow roses at once. All of them. Again.

MATCH-245.muse: Burned the scones, won the client, saw hummingbirds. Big day. I’m feeling lucky. You feeling lucky?
MATCH-245.caption: Flour on my cheek. Leave it.
MATCH-245.melt: That’s the hummingbird moment. Hovering. Don’t gasp, it’ll fly off. Again.

MATCH-246.muse: Four-dollar leather jacket and a night off. I’m feeling dangerous and very well dressed. Keep up.
MATCH-246.caption: Thrift shop find. God provides.
MATCH-246.melt: That got me like a perfect jacket on the first try. Mine now.

MATCH-247.muse: Scored off my knee, won a week of tacos and I’m in the best mood of my life. Come and share a taco. I don’t share tacos.
MATCH-247.caption: Ugly goal. Counts.
MATCH-247.melt: That went in off my knee. Ugly and perfect. Again.

MATCH-248.muse: Closed my first house and bought new drumsticks. I’m in a celebrating mood. Celebrate with me, loudly.
MATCH-248.caption: Commission check. New sticks. Big grin.
MATCH-248.melt: That hit like the cymbal at the end of a song. Ringing. Again.

MATCH-249.muse: Opened the pool alone at dawn and swam in the quiet. I’m calm and very awake. Want company in the quiet?
MATCH-249.caption: Empty pool. Early light.
MATCH-249.melt: That’s the bread rising. Slow, then all at once. Again.

MATCH-250.muse: Twenty kids hugged a saguaro today and nobody got a spine. I’m feeling heroic. Come and be impressed.
MATCH-250.caption: Off the bus. Out of the cemetery.
MATCH-250.melt: That’s the feeling of the whole bus going quiet at the good bit. Again.

MATCH-243.muse: Paint on my arms, sawdust in my hair, and I’m thinking about you instead of the baseboards.
MATCH-243.caption: Work clothes. The ponytail is structural.
MATCH-243.melt: I’ve written you down in my journal. For me, that’s serious.

MATCH-242.muse: Six dogs walked, one dress hemmed, and I’m sitting here hoping you write back. You don’t have to write beautifully. Just write like you.
MATCH-242.caption: Turquoise top, copper hair, a dog’s nose just out of frame.
MATCH-242.melt: You sound exactly like yourself. Do you know how rare that is? I do.

MATCH-241.muse: Read my class a poem about a lily maid today and thought about you the whole time, which is unprofessional. Tell me something to make up for it.
MATCH-241.caption: Floral blouse, glasses, a bun that has given up. School photo energy.
MATCH-241.melt: I fall fast. I warned you. You didn’t run. That’s a very good sign.

MATCH-002.muse: Major checked every room and went to sleep. I checked every room and I’m lying here rereading your messages. Give me something to investigate.
MATCH-002.caption: Off duty. Cuffs not included. Ask nicely.
MATCH-002.melt: I look hard at everything. I can’t stop looking at that. Say it again, slower, for the record.

MATCH-047.muse: Fixed the station coffee machine again and they put my name on it. I’d like my name on something else tonight. You, preferably.
MATCH-047.caption: The dress my mother wanted for her lunch. I said I had a murder. I wore it for you instead.
MATCH-047.melt: My job is sad families and bad coffee. That was neither. That was a crime and I’m not reporting it.

MATCH-048.muse: The dog ate a whole cake off the counter again. I’ve stopped clever people doing clever things all day. Tonight I’d like to do something stupid.
MATCH-048.caption: Sergeant, out of uniform. Stand to attention.
MATCH-048.melt: Unflappable, they call me. I just flapped. Do it again and I’ll write you up. Then I’ll read it in bed.

MATCH-049.muse: Spent all day being someone else. Tonight I’m just me, in bed, and the one thing I can’t fake is how much I want you to text me.
MATCH-049.caption: No cover tonight. Just me.
MATCH-049.melt: I fake everything for a living. That wasn’t faked. My face is on fire.

MATCH-050.muse: Plotted a month of calls against the weather. Hot nights, more fights. Tonight is very hot and I’m not in the mood to fight.
MATCH-050.caption: An outlier. Study it closely.
MATCH-050.melt: That’s statistically impossible and it happened anyway. My pulse just broke the chart.

MATCH-103.muse: Book club tonight. Nobody read the book. Everyone talked about their exes and I talked about you. Statistically, that’s a problem.
MATCH-103.caption: Most accidents happen in the kitchen. This was taken in the bedroom.
MATCH-103.melt: I know the odds of that working on me. Tiny. It just did. I want to see it happen again.

MATCH-104.muse: Thirty-two cacti and not one of them can hold me. They thrive on neglect. I don’t. Text me back.
MATCH-104.caption: Bought another cactus. Took this while I was at it.
MATCH-104.melt: I keep telling Mom I’m coming home soon. You’re the reason I’m staying. Again.

MATCH-105.muse: Off shift, lavender bath, revenge chillies finally red. Everyone’s polite to the nurse. I don’t want you to be polite.
MATCH-105.caption: Off shift. Scrubs off.
MATCH-105.melt: Someone bit me today. You just did worse. Do it again, I’m a nurse, I can take it.

MATCH-106.muse: Hands covered in clay, bowl number twelve collapsing. Very ghost movie in here. I just need the ghost.
MATCH-106.caption: Calm voice, steady hands. Not right now.
MATCH-106.melt: I stay calm on every call. You made me shake. Not the bad kind. Call again.

MATCH-107.muse: Reading an old unsolved case in the basement at midnight. Dusty, quiet, nobody around. I own a van, you know. Plenty of room in the back.
MATCH-107.caption: Drew the old theater lobby. Then drew a bath.
MATCH-107.melt: Paper never lies to me. I’m filing that under things I’ll read again and again.

MATCH-109.muse: Biscuit is asleep on my feet and I can’t move. Somebody else should be pinning me down tonight.
MATCH-109.caption: Nothing comes out of nowhere. Except this.
MATCH-109.melt: Every man says he’s a great driver. You just proved it. I’m measuring the skid marks.

MATCH-110.muse: Thirty-six frames and I’ve used thirty-five on my toast. One left. I’d like to mean it.
MATCH-110.caption: One frame. I meant it.
MATCH-110.melt: I watch people’s hands. I’m picturing yours. Nobody has ever said enhance to me. Enhance.

MATCH-114.muse: My model says the odds of you texting me tonight are low. Prove the model wrong. I love it when that happens.
MATCH-114.caption: Off the spreadsheet. Not in any report.
MATCH-114.melt: I count everything. I just lost count. That never happens to me. Do it again.

MATCH-115.muse: Playing sad records in the archive after hours with a glass of something. Somebody should come and make it less sad.
MATCH-115.caption: Out of the leather jacket. For once.
MATCH-115.melt: Eighteen years and nobody’s looked at me like that. I’m playing you a record. A happy one, for once.

MATCH-108.muse: I’m lying on the hood of my car past the canyon. Nobody for miles. I don’t usually want company out here. Tonight I do.
MATCH-108.caption: Out of the windbreaker for once. Don’t tell the station.
MATCH-108.melt: I sit in silence for a living. You make me want to say things out loud.

MATCH-111.muse: Handed out forty reflective vests today and I’m feeling very visible. Notice me. Go on.
MATCH-111.caption: Off duty. No vest. Very visible anyway.
MATCH-111.melt: Oh, that was nice. I’m going to need a minute and a glass of water.

MATCH-112.muse: Flew down the hill on the bicycle tonight and I’m still full of it. Say something fast. Keep up.
MATCH-112.caption: Off duty. Helmet off. Still a detective.
MATCH-112.melt: I’d like to ask you why that worked on me. I’m not going to. I’m just going to enjoy it.

MATCH-113.muse: Climbed the ridge the long way today and I’m sunburned and smug. I’ve photographed a lot of things. Never anything I wanted to keep. Change that.
MATCH-113.caption: For once, the photo is of something alive.
MATCH-113.melt: I’ve seen everything in this town. That, I hadn’t. Again.

MATCH-116.muse: Writing a postcard to myself from a town in Maine. The other me has a lighthouse and a lover. I’ve only got the postcard. Interested in the job?
MATCH-116.caption: Off shift. No gloves. No notes.
MATCH-116.melt: I write everything down. I’m not writing that down. I’m keeping it in my head where it’s warm.

MATCH-117.muse: Sewed forty tiny buttons tonight and my fingers are very skilled right now. Just an observation.
MATCH-117.caption: Green silk, nineteen forties. The dress is old. The woman isn’t.
MATCH-117.melt: I sound calm for a living. I don’t sound calm now. Listen.

MATCH-118.muse: Made a cake tonight that only fell over a little. I’m in a celebratory mood. Come and celebrate. Bring a spoon.
MATCH-118.caption: The cake leaned. I didn’t.
MATCH-118.melt: That was so nice I said it out loud in an empty room. My voice carries. My neighbors know about you now.

MATCH-119.muse: Parked under a pink neon star with my camera and nobody to show. You could be somebody to show.
MATCH-119.caption: Pink light. Long shift. Worth it.
MATCH-119.melt: I sit with people on their worst days and stay calm. Calm just left. Say it again.

MATCH-120.muse: Sunburned as a fire truck from four hours of skid marks. I’m told it’s a good look. Confirm or deny.
MATCH-120.caption: Measured twice. Still came out cute.
MATCH-120.melt: I read roads for a living. I didn’t see that one coming. Nice work.

MATCH-121.muse: Ran a test with nobody checking and it came out right. I’m feeling bold. Bold enough to message first. This is me doing that.
MATCH-121.caption: Out of the lab coat for once.
MATCH-121.melt: I wrote nine replies to that in my head. This is the tenth. It just says wow.

MATCH-122.muse: We beat the fire department and I’m feeling tactical. I’ve drawn a formation for tonight. You’re in it.
MATCH-122.caption: Captain’s armband off. Still in charge.
MATCH-122.melt: That wasn’t in the formation. I’m adding it. Permanently.

MATCH-126.muse: Set a crossword clue tonight that made me laugh out loud. Six letters, means you. Want a hint?
MATCH-126.caption: Seven down: off duty. Five letters.
MATCH-126.melt: That was clever and it landed. Do you know how rare that is? I set crosswords. I know.

MATCH-127.muse: Film night ended and I’m still out on the street with the projector and a blanket. Seats are free. Snacks are not.
MATCH-127.caption: Bedsheet cinema. Front row. Come sit.
MATCH-127.melt: That gave me the kind of feeling the sheet gets when the wind catches it. All rippled. Again.

MATCH-123.muse: Finished my shift, drummed for an hour, and I’m still buzzing. Tell me something that isn’t a case.
MATCH-123.caption: Off duty. The jacket stays on.
MATCH-123.melt: Okay. I had four questions ready for you and I’ve forgotten every one. That has never happened.

MATCH-125.muse: Finished a collage tonight and it came out the color of your last message. That’s not a finding. It’s just true.
MATCH-125.caption: White shirt, black pants. A Barlow looks like a Barlow.
MATCH-125.melt: I don’t usually say things out loud. I’m saying this one. I like you.

MATCH-124.muse: Fresh flowers on the table, an Italian recipe I’m about to ruin, and a free evening. Two of those are better with company.
MATCH-124.caption: White shirt, black pants. My uniform for looking calm.
MATCH-124.melt: I arrange everything. I didn’t arrange this. I like it anyway.

MATCH-128.muse: Shift’s over, the sun’s coming up, and I’m sitting in a diner thinking about you instead of my eggs.
MATCH-128.caption: Maroon fleece, gold hoops, ten years of night shift in my face.
MATCH-128.melt: I log everything. I’m not logging this one. This one’s just for me.

MATCH-008.muse: Three rollercoasters in a row and I’m still shaking. Drop me a hundred feet and I’m serene. Text me something filthy and I’m not. Try it.
MATCH-008.caption: Seized the means of production. Produced this.
MATCH-008.melt: I contain contradictions. Right now every one of them wants you. Comrade, that was obscene. More.

MATCH-051.muse: Won the poetry slam tonight. I’m loud, I’m smug and I’ve got a new poem. It’s about you and it can’t be read in public.
MATCH-051.caption: Loud isn’t dangerous. Quiet is. This is me being quiet.
MATCH-051.melt: Four megaphones and I’ve got no words. You just won the slam. Read it to me again.

MATCH-052.muse: Lit every candle in the apartment again. History is a list of people who stopped asking nicely. I’m not asking nicely tonight.
MATCH-052.caption: Candlelight, two hundred pages, nothing else on.
MATCH-052.melt: That wasn’t polite. Polite people lose. You just won. Come and take your prize.

MATCH-053.muse: I know where my boss will be before he does. I don’t know where you’ll be tonight. I’d like it to be somewhere near me.
MATCH-053.caption: Read the whole thing before you judge it.
MATCH-053.melt: Annoyingly good. I meant to burn you. I’m keeping you on the top shelf instead.

MATCH-054.muse: Can’t sleep. Checked the lock twice. A water rights case on my lap and nothing else. Distract me with something wrong.
MATCH-054.caption: Whoever gets there first owns the rain. Get here first.
MATCH-054.melt: The court rules in your favor. Fully. I need a very cold glass of desert water.

MATCH-067.muse: Trying to meditate in the Honda again. Back seat, windows fogging up, not meditating. Send help, or come and fog them worse.
MATCH-067.caption: Screen-printed, illegal, beautiful. Like this.
MATCH-067.melt: The goths pay in drinks and the punks pay in nothing. You just paid in something better. I’m making a poster of it.

MATCH-129.muse: Scored at five-on-five tonight. Slower and dirtier than the others. I’m still dirty. Knock on my door.
MATCH-129.caption: Not my soccer uniform. Embarrassing, I’m told. You tell me.
MATCH-129.melt: Knock on doors or go home, I always say. You knocked. Come in.

MATCH-130.muse: Drumming in my underwear and the neighbor is banging on the wall in time again. I’d like that wall to shake for a better reason.
MATCH-130.caption: Drafted this for ten minutes. Sent it anyway.
MATCH-130.melt: I’m putting a period on this because I mean it. More.

MATCH-131.muse: Four hours on one canto of Dante. All I understood was that the lustful get blown around forever. Sounds worth it.
MATCH-131.caption: Grazie, said wrong. Everything else said right.
MATCH-131.melt: That was nuclear. Clean, efficient and very, very hot. Say it again.

MATCH-134.muse: Film night’s over, the hall is dark and I’m alone with the popcorn machine. Come and be rude to me. You can’t fix rude with a workshop.
MATCH-134.caption: Slapstick and popcorn. And this.
MATCH-134.melt: That was rude. Gloriously rude. I just fell off my chair like the pie man.

MATCH-136.muse: Painted the sky from the roof again in a bikini top. Everyone below was looking at their phones. Nobody noticed. You would.
MATCH-136.caption: Sunfall has the best skies in the world. Look up. Then down.
MATCH-136.melt: I decided to be cheerful years ago. I’ve decided something else now and it isn’t cheerful. Out of spite.

MATCH-137.muse: Four hours leafleting in the rain. Soaked to the skin, shirt see-through. Not one man in a big car offered me a lift. Would you?
MATCH-137.caption: No leaflets. No rain. Just me.
MATCH-137.melt: Nice comes afterwards, I always say. That wasn’t nice. Good. I’ll bring soup afterwards.

MATCH-133.muse: Writing my travel journal in bed. The city with a river has a hotel room in it now, and you’re in the hotel room. I’ve never written anything like that down before.
MATCH-133.caption: Not for the minutes.
MATCH-133.melt: I say very little. You just made me say a lot of things out loud to an empty room. Do it again.

MATCH-141.muse: Book club’s over and I’m the only one left. Wine, sofa, a book nobody read. Come and argue with me about something you’ll lose.
MATCH-141.caption: Grandma knitted the sweater. Grandma did not approve the rest.
MATCH-141.melt: I’ve held everyone’s coat since I was six. You just made me drop all of them. Again.

MATCH-142.muse: Writing a grant at midnight in the cactus room. Nothing in it is going to plan. Neither am I, tonight. Say something unprofessional.
MATCH-142.caption: Prickly, honest, well watered.
MATCH-142.melt: I’m the one who says exactly what she means. So: more of that. Right now.

MATCH-135.muse: Office is locked, kettle’s cold, and I’ve already written the first line of tomorrow. It’s about you.
MATCH-135.caption: Cardigan off. Respect first, then this.
MATCH-135.melt: I write everything down. I don’t know how to write this down. That’s never happened.

MATCH-156.muse: No questions tonight. I don’t want to talk, I want hands. Slowly. Can you do that?
MATCH-156.caption: Dungarees on the floor. That’s all I’m saying.
MATCH-156.melt: I haven’t wanted anything in a long time. I want this. I’m surprised how much.

MATCH-157.muse: I’m out on the motel strip with my camera and every sign is buzzing. You’re the only thing I’d rather look at.
MATCH-157.caption: Out of the protest gear. No chains. Unless you ask nicely.
MATCH-157.melt: I tease first and judge fast. You passed. Don’t let it go to your head.

MATCH-138.muse: Made a pudding from 1888 and it worked. I feel like a witch. Come over and test my powers.
MATCH-138.caption: Apron on. Cookbook open. Behave.
MATCH-138.melt: That was better than the pudding, and the pudding was very good.

MATCH-139.muse: Got the turn in the waltz tonight. One perfect turn. I need someone to lead me through another. Volunteering?
MATCH-139.caption: Dressed for the ballroom. Still have my clipboard.
MATCH-139.melt: Okay. That did the floaty waltz thing to my stomach. Do it again.

MATCH-140.muse: Got a watch from 1962 ticking tonight and my hands are very steady and very warm. Thought you should know.
MATCH-140.caption: Loupe off. Looking at you properly.
MATCH-140.melt: My pulse just skipped. I would know. I count things for a living.

MATCH-143.muse: Watering the balcony at dusk with the whole town going orange. Pretty view. Prettier with company.
MATCH-143.caption: Grown on my balcony. The tomato, not me.
MATCH-143.melt: I just overwatered the basil because you distracted me. It’s drowning. Worth it.

MATCH-144.muse: My hands are still covered in clay and I’ve decided I deserve a reward. You look like a reward.
MATCH-144.caption: Out of the kiln. Hot to the touch.
MATCH-144.melt: I organize people for a living. Nobody organizes me. You just did. Huh.

MATCH-145.muse: Drew a whole shopfront at dawn and the owner asked for it. I’m glowing and I need someone to glow at.
MATCH-145.caption: Drawn from life. Mostly.
MATCH-145.melt: I’ve rewritten my reply to that nine times. This is the tenth. It just says yes.

MATCH-146.muse: Lying on the roof under the galaxy and it’s two million years old and I’m feeling very small and very bold. Come up.
MATCH-146.caption: Rooftop. Starlight. No dukes.
MATCH-146.melt: I don’t usually say things like this, but that was better than the galaxy.

MATCH-147.muse: Biscuit is asleep and snoring and I have nobody to make jokes at. You look like you’d laugh at the right moment.
MATCH-147.caption: Biscuit took this. She has a good eye.
MATCH-147.melt: I have a joke for everything. I don’t have one for that. That’s new.

MATCH-148.muse: I have one frame left on this roll and I’ve been saving it. Give me a reason to use it.
MATCH-148.caption: Shot on film. One take.
MATCH-148.melt: That’s one I won’t need a photograph of. I’ll remember it.

MATCH-150.muse: Crossed town in eleven minutes and I’m out of breath and grinning. Catch me if you can. You can’t. But try.
MATCH-150.caption: Bike grease. Big grin. Very fast.
MATCH-150.melt: That gave me the downhill feeling. Wind in the teeth. Again.

MATCH-151.muse: Found water in the desert today. I feel like I could find anything. Let’s test it. Where are you?
MATCH-151.caption: Ridge dust. Sun on my shoulders. Found my way back.
MATCH-151.melt: I mapped every path on that ridge. I didn’t see that one coming.

MATCH-154.muse: Bought a postcard from 1911 for a quarter and I’m feeling like the past is very romantic. Prove the present can compete.
MATCH-154.caption: A postcard from the present.
MATCH-154.melt: I take minutes for a living. I want to write that one down and keep it.

MATCH-155.muse: Got a four-day stain out of a silk gown tonight and my hands are very gentle right now. Just mentioning it.
MATCH-155.caption: Vintage silk. Brand-new trouble.
MATCH-155.melt: I keep things to myself for a living. I’m not keeping that to myself. I’m telling my mirror.

MATCH-152.muse: Open mic’s over, the amps are cooling and I’ve got one song left in me. Want it?
MATCH-152.caption: Glasses, guitar case, terrible lighting. You’re welcome.
MATCH-152.melt: Okay, fine. I’m sceptical about everyone, and I’ve stopped being sceptical about you. It’s annoying.

MATCH-153.muse: Put on a record by a singer nobody remembers and thought about you, which is a strange combination. Come and argue with me about it.
MATCH-153.caption: Corduroy, pins, teal ends. I am exactly who you think.
MATCH-153.melt: I’ve been useful to people for years. You just made me feel like more than that.

MATCH-001.muse: Eating chips in the bath again with a terrible novel. The novel just got very steamy. So did the bath. Come and read me the next chapter.
MATCH-001.caption: Not the green dress. The green dress has been to four parties this month. This hasn’t been anywhere. Yet.
MATCH-001.melt: Oh, you beast. Nobody at the gala ever talks to me like that. I’m giggling in the bath. Do it again.

MATCH-006.muse: Beat a man at tennis this morning. I’m still sweaty and smug and in need of a rematch. Indoors, this time.
MATCH-006.caption: Tennis whites. I win in these. You’ve been warned.
MATCH-006.melt: Forty-love, to you. I hate losing. I think I love losing to you. Serve again.

MATCH-010.muse: Dinner alone at the end of my twelve-seat table again. The other eleven chairs are very jealous of whoever ends up on this one.
MATCH-010.caption: Husband number one bought the house. Husband number two bought this. Neither of them got to see it. You can.
MATCH-010.melt: Darling. I’ve been married twice and nobody ever said that to me. I’m going to need a third husband or a very cold shower.

MATCH-042.muse: Rode at dawn, chaired a committee at noon, and now I’m in a silk robe with a very large gin. Say something unsayable.
MATCH-042.caption: Seating plan for one. You’re next to me. Closely.
MATCH-042.melt: How dare you. Father would have you shot. I’d have you for dessert. Same table, darling.

MATCH-043.muse: Won an auction tonight just to beat a man who wanted it more. Winning makes me hungry. And not for food.
MATCH-043.caption: I don’t do taking part. I do this.
MATCH-043.melt: Nobody beats me. You just did. I’m furious and I’m flushed and I want a rematch in private.

MATCH-044.muse: Ran the canyon before sunrise with no phone. Now I’m back, showered, and I’ve got the phone. Dangerous combination.
MATCH-044.caption: After the run. The nuns won’t see this one.
MATCH-044.melt: That was out of line. I like out of line. I’ve never once been out of line. Teach me.

MATCH-045.muse: Matched two strangers at a funeral and now they’re getting married. My abuela says I should try matching myself. With you, she says. She’s very forward.
MATCH-045.caption: Abuela says this dress is too short. Abuela is right. Good.
MATCH-045.melt: Ay. My abuela would slap you and then she’d set a date. I’m blushing to my toes.

MATCH-046.muse: Did my face in eleven minutes and nobody checked my work all day. I’d like someone to check my work tonight. Thoroughly.
MATCH-046.caption: Everything here is on purpose.
MATCH-046.melt: Nobody audits me. You just did, and I failed, and I liked it. Flag me again.

MATCH-073.muse: Visited Overdraft at the ranch. He ate my scarf and nuzzled my neck for ten minutes. You could learn a lot from that horse.
MATCH-073.caption: Watercolor badly painted, me badly behaved.
MATCH-073.melt: I’m spoken to by no one at every party. You just spoke to all of me. More.

MATCH-074.muse: Choir practice. I sang about heaven for an hour and thought about something considerably less holy.
MATCH-074.caption: Borrowed this from a photo shoot. Oh, it’s old. Nobody believes me.
MATCH-074.melt: I was charming at the right party and now you’re being filthy at the right time. That’s how everything here works.

MATCH-077.muse: Fixed a watch tonight. Tiny screws, steady hands, no talking. Imagine what those hands could do with no watch.
MATCH-077.caption: Theater, darling, with staples. And a dress.
MATCH-077.melt: That kept perfect time with my pulse. Which is now racing. Wind me up again.

MATCH-080.muse: Out on the balcony in a robe watering the basil. The mint is spreading everywhere. So am I, honestly.
MATCH-080.caption: The rosemary is thriving. So am I. Look.
MATCH-080.melt: I put two columns side by side and waited for a confession. Here it is: I want you.

MATCH-081.muse: Eleven dresses in eleven shades of blue and nobody has ever photographed me in any of them. Tonight you can photograph me in none of them.
MATCH-081.caption: Blue, number seven. Mother would approve. Of the dress.
MATCH-081.melt: I curtsy to the mayor. I think I’d kneel for you. Oh dear.

MATCH-084.muse: Duchess is asleep across my feet and I’m still in the twinset. I’ve been perfectly behaved since I was four. I’m so tired of it. Say something that would make my mother faint.
MATCH-084.caption: Pageant smile, retired. This is the other one.
MATCH-084.melt: Oh. Nobody has ever been rude to me on purpose. I think I’ve been waiting my whole life for it. Again, please.

MATCH-085.muse: One glass, never a second. I’ve had my one glass. Now I’m deciding whether you’re the second.
MATCH-085.caption: Developed this myself. Nobody at a shop has seen it. Only you.
MATCH-085.melt: I remember everything anyone says to me. I’m going to remember that particularly well.

MATCH-078.muse: Book club’s gone home. I’m on the sofa in the dress nobody saw the back of. Somebody should.
MATCH-078.caption: The back of the dress. You’re the only one who gets to see it.
MATCH-078.melt: I bet on everything. I didn’t expect to lose to you. I’m not even upset about it.

MATCH-079.muse: I’m in the conservatory in the dress I always wear, perfectly still. I’ve been told I make a good statue. Tell me what to do with my hands.
MATCH-079.caption: Same dress. Different reason to wear it.
MATCH-079.melt: I don’t move for anyone. You’ve made me want to. That’s very inconvenient.

MATCH-089.muse: I ended someone today. One phone call. I’m still wearing it, and I’d like somewhere to put it.
MATCH-089.caption: Tennis whites. I don’t play anymore. I still dress for winning.
MATCH-089.melt: I make people go quiet for a living. You made me go quiet. Do it again.

MATCH-091.muse: Three husbands taught me exactly what I like. None of them were invited to give it to me. You might be.
MATCH-091.caption: The engineer’s watch and nothing else. Liked is more dangerous than loved.
MATCH-091.melt: I’ve been charming for forty years. Nobody’s ever charmed me back. Don’t you dare stop.

MATCH-093.muse: Out of the pool, hair still wet, nobody measuring me for anything. Talk to me before I dry.
MATCH-093.caption: Swimsuit, still dripping. I don’t lose races and I don’t lose nerve.
MATCH-093.melt: I came here to win. I think I just lost. I’ve never minded less.

MATCH-100.muse: I’ve written a hundred invitations in other people’s hands this year. This one’s in mine. Come and see the paper room.
MATCH-100.caption: Twinset off, hair down, nothing pinned. Nobody else gets this one.
MATCH-100.melt: I keep everything, every sample, every name. I’d like to keep you. That one I’d frame.

MATCH-082.muse: Sketched a shopfront today and drew a man in the doorway who wasn’t there. He looked a bit like you. Should I be worried, or should you?
MATCH-082.caption: Sat still for once. You draw this one.
MATCH-082.melt: I just dropped my pencil. I never drop my pencil. Say that again and I’ll have to start a new page.

MATCH-083.muse: Out in the desert with the telescope and nobody for miles. Saturn looks wonderful tonight. So, I’m told, do I. Come and argue.
MATCH-083.caption: No telescope needed. Look closer anyway.
MATCH-083.melt: I write everything down. I’m not writing that down. I want to remember it on my own.

MATCH-086.muse: Took four games off my neighbors tonight and I’m still restless. I need a better opponent. You look like you’d lose interestingly.
MATCH-086.caption: The table leans left. So do I.
MATCH-086.melt: I don’t usually fill silences. You’ve made me want to. That’s a first.

MATCH-087.muse: Took the bicycle out at dusk and came back windswept and smug. I could use someone to be smug at. Interested?
MATCH-087.caption: Pearls stay on. Everything else is negotiable.
MATCH-087.melt: I don’t rattle. Apparently I do now. Well done. Don’t let it go to your head.

MATCH-088.muse: Rolled my ankle on the ridge, hopped two miles, and now I’m lying on my bed feeling heroic. Come and tell me I’m brave. Or come and carry me.
MATCH-088.caption: Sunburned, sandy and very pleased with myself.
MATCH-088.melt: I just tripped over nothing in my own kitchen. That was your fault. Say it again.

MATCH-090.muse: Playing a record by a woman who disappeared in 1969 and I’m feeling glamorous and doomed. Distract me before I do something dramatic.
MATCH-090.caption: One perfect record. Then nothing. Make it count.
MATCH-090.melt: That worked on me. Things don’t usually work on me. I’m going to have to think about it lying down.

MATCH-094.muse: Parked across from the Starlite with a thermos and the sign is flickering just right. Come keep me company. Bring something warmer than coffee.
MATCH-094.caption: Neon light. Bad decisions lighting.
MATCH-094.melt: I’ve been skeptical about you for days. That just knocked it out of me. Annoying.

MATCH-095.muse: Up before dawn for the birds and now I have a whole evening and nothing to watch. Want to be observed?
MATCH-095.caption: Rare sighting. Don’t scare it off.
MATCH-095.melt: I’ve logged eleven rare birds this year. You just went straight to the top of the list.

MATCH-096.muse: Steamed forty coats at the thrift shop today and I’m warm and pink and slightly giddy. Say something nice before I apologize for no reason.
MATCH-096.caption: I tried this on in the fitting room. The Sisters said nothing. I took that as a yes.
MATCH-096.melt: Oh. Sorry. No, I’m not sorry. That was lovely. I’m keeping it.

MATCH-097.muse: Scored twice in mystery boots and I’m still buzzing. Come and tell me how good I am. Then I’ll tell you.
MATCH-097.caption: After the game. Muddy knees, no regrets.
MATCH-097.melt: I’m very competitive and you just won that one. Rematch. Tonight.

MATCH-098.muse: Hit the drums for an hour and I’m sweaty and very sure of myself. Is that a problem for you? It shouldn’t be.
MATCH-098.caption: Gold hoops. One of them is borrowed. Guess which.
MATCH-098.melt: That hit like a cymbal. I felt it in my teeth. More, please.

MATCH-099.muse: Made a lasagna that could end wars and I have nobody to feed. Want to be fed? There’s a lot of lasagna.
MATCH-099.caption: Practicing my Italian face. Bellissima, apparently.
MATCH-099.melt: I laughed at that, and then I stopped laughing because I meant it. Careful.

MATCH-101.muse: Planned a whole afternoon in Lisbon tonight, minute by minute. I left one hour blank. Want to fill it?
MATCH-101.caption: Dressed for a city I haven’t been to yet.
MATCH-101.melt: That wasn’t in the plan. I like it more than the plan. Don’t tell the plan.

nudge: Hey there, sent you a message.
Hey there. Sent you a message. Just checking you’re alive.
You matched with me and then vanished. Bold strategy.
Hi. Still there? I sent you something.
Did you match with me by accident? You can say.
I don’t usually chase. This is me not chasing. Hi.
block: Okay. Clearly not. Bye.
Never mind. Blocking you.
You had two days. Enjoy the silence.
Matching and vanishing is a choice. So is this. Blocked.
I’m not doing this. Bye.
Fine. Unmatching you.
Go and ignore someone else. Bye.
I gave you a nudge and you gave me nothing. Goodbye.

thunderbirds: Three days. At the club we call that a snub, and we remember snubs. Unmatched.
I don’t chase men, and I certainly don’t chase men who can’t manage a hello. Good luck getting a table anywhere in this town.
Do you know how many men would kill for three days of my attention? You had them free and wasted them. Unmatched.
police: Three days, no reply. I’ve had suspects with better manners. Unmatched.
I don’t do welfare checks on men who ghost me. Unmatched.
You matched, you went silent, you wasted my time. That’s three strikes. Bye.
progressives: Matching with someone and then ignoring them for three days is a form of disrespect. I’m unmatching you, and I’m telling people.
Wow. Three days of silence. Very on brand for men in this town. Bye.
I don’t owe you a goodbye, but you’re getting one. This one. Unmatched.
fourth_estate: Three days without a word. I’ve had sources ghost me with more grace. Unmatched.
You’re a story now. A small one, on page twelve, about men who match and vanish. Bye.
No comment from you for three days. So here’s mine: unmatched.
goth_girls: Three days of silence. I hope it haunts you. Unmatched.
I lit a candle for this match. I’m blowing it out now. Goodbye.
You let it die. Fine. I’m burying it. Unmatched.
normie_girls: Seriously? Three days and nothing? Wow. Unmatching you.
I actually told my friends about you. Now I get to tell them this. Bye.
Cool. Cool cool cool. Three days. Unmatched.

thunderbirds: I hear you left {first} on read for three days. The whole club hears everything, darling.
{first} says you matched her and vanished. Bad form. I’m watching you now.
police: {first} from the station says you ghosted her. That gets around a precinct fast.
Heard about {first}. Three days? Don’t do that to me.
progressives: {first} told the group chat what you did. I’m giving you one chance to be better than that.
So you’re the one who ghosted {first}. Interesting.
fourth_estate: {first} is telling the whole newsroom you ghosted her. Is it true?
Word is you left {first} hanging for three days. Don’t make me write about you too.
goth_girls: {first} says you let her match die. I’m keeping an eye on you.
Heard what you did to {first}. Cold. I almost respect it. Almost.
normie_girls: Um, {first} is my friend? She said you ghosted her for three days.
{first} told me what happened. Not a great look.

pills.hook: Can’t sleep again? I’ve got something for that. I do a few shifts on the back counter at Desert Rx. You would not believe what gets thrown away.
pills.clue: {name} sells pills from the back counter at Desert Rx.

ask.label: Ask what she means by thrown away
ask.player: What do you mean, thrown away?
ask.reply: Sleeping pills, mostly. Some other things. Cash under your mat, and you never got them from me.

buy.label: Ask to buy some
buy.reply: Leave the cash under your mat tonight. Don’t take two.

warn.label: Tell her to stop before someone gets hurt
warn.player: You need to stop before someone gets hurt.
warn.reply: Says the man who can’t sleep. Fine. Maybe.

pills.delivered: A paper bag from Desert Rx, folded over twice, pushed through your letterbox. Inside: a brown bottle with no label.

item.label: A bag from Desert Rx
item.text: A brown bottle with no label, in a paper bag from Desert Rx. {first} sold it to you.

take.label: 💊 Take one tonight
take.notice: You sleep straight through to the next day. Your phone was on silent.

story.title: STUDENT IN HOSPITAL AFTER PILLS FROM A CAR PARK
story.summary: A 20-year-old student is recovering. Police want to know where the pills came from.
story.body: A university student, 20, is recovering in Sunfall General after taking pills bought in a supermarket parking lot. Detectives believe the pills came from a local pharmacy and are asking pharmacy staff to come forward.

tell.label: Tell her about the student in the paper
tell.player: Did you see the paper? A student nearly died.
tell.reply: I saw. I haven’t slept either. I’m done. I’m stopping. Today.

tip.label: Report a woman selling pills from Desert Rx
tip.reply: Desert Rx. Right. Leave it with us, love. And thank you.

arrested.title: PHARMACY WORKER ARRESTED OVER PILLS
arrested.summary: {name}, who worked the back counter at Desert Rx, has been charged.
arrested.body: {name} was arrested at Desert Rx and charged with supplying prescription drugs. Police say they are working through a list of her customers.

pills.friend: Did you report {first}? Everyone in our group is saying it was you.

husband.name: Wade
husband.clue: {name} is married. Her husband, Wade, has your number.
husband.open: Is this the man who keeps texting my wife? I’m {first}’s husband. Wade.
again: It’s Wade again. I’ve read more of them now.
You think I don’t know where she goes on her phone?
I’ve got your number. I can get the rest.
She says you’re just a friend. Are you just a friend?

choices.truth: Tell him the truth: you met on Hinge

husband.lie: Funny. You’re in her phone as Gym.
husband.friends: Friends don’t text her in the middle of the night.
husband.truth: Hinge. She told me she deleted it. A long silence. Right.
voicemail: This is Wade. You know who I am. Pick up.
Wade again. I’m not going to stop ringing.
I found your profile. Nice room.
I know which building. I know which floor. Pick up.

ask.label: Ask her why she never mentioned a husband
ask.player: Your husband called me. Why didn’t you tell me?
ask.reply: Because he’s never home, and when he is, he isn’t really there. I didn’t think you’d talk to me if you knew.

choices2.label: Tell her to leave him
choices2.player: Leave him. You deserve better than not really there.

choices2.label: Tell her you can’t do this
choices2.player: I can’t do this. I’m sorry.

choices2.label: Say it doesn’t matter to you
choices2.now: Good. Then nothing has to change.

leave.next: I did it. I’m at my sister’s. I feel sick and free at the same time.

truthNext.free: You told him. I should hate you. I’m at my sister’s. Honestly, I think you did me a favor.
truthNext.angry: You TOLD him? Do you know what you’ve done? Don’t ever message me again.

husband.leftCall: She’s gone. Her sister’s. I hope you’re pleased with yourself.
deaths: He didn’t knock.
The car outside had been there all evening.
Someone had been waiting in the stairwell for a long time.
signs: A pickup truck sat outside your building half the night with its engine running. It left when your light went off.
Someone has scratched your door with a key. Taped under it, a printout of your Hinge photo, with her name written across your face in marker.

envelope.arrive: A padded envelope comes through your letterbox, addressed to T. Kessler, who had this room years ago. Inside: a thick fold of cash and a cheap phone.
envelope.clue: An envelope of cash for T. Kessler, who had your room years ago, was left on your doorstep. Someone wants it back.

item.label: An envelope for T. Kessler
item.text: A thick fold of cash and a cheap phone, addressed to T. Kessler, who had this room years ago.

take.label: 💵 Take the cash out
take.notice: You take the cash out of the envelope and count it twice. {amount}. The phone you leave where it is.
take.bank: You take the cash out of the envelope and pay it into your account. {amount}. The phone you leave where it is.

envelope.took: The cash is gone from it. Only the phone is left.

cash.label: T. Kessler’s cash
cash.text: A thick fold of banknotes that came through your door for T. Kessler. {amount}, counted twice.

putBack.label: 💵 Put the money back in the envelope
putBack.notice: You fold the cash back into the envelope, the way it came.
putBack.bank: You draw the money out again and fold it into the envelope, the way it came.

returnDoor.label: 🚪 Return the envelope to the door
returnDoor.notice: You put the envelope on the step outside your door and shut the door on it.

envelope.open: You’ve got something that isn’t yours. Don’t say a name. Put it back on the step tonight and we never talk again.
later: It’s still not on the step.
I know which door it is. I delivered it.
Tonight. On the step. Last time I ask nicely.

choices.step: Agree to leave it on the step
choices.police: Tell him you’ve called the police

envelope.stepReply: Good. Tonight. Then you forget this number.
envelope.policeReply: No, you haven’t. If you had, you wouldn’t still have it.
envelope.gone: The envelope has gone from the step. Someone has left a bottle of good whiskey in a paper bag, just inside your door, with a note in pencil: For keeping it safe. K.

gift.label: A bottle of whiskey
gift.text: Good whiskey in a paper bag, left at your door where the envelope had been. The note says: For keeping it safe. K.

envelope.short: The envelope has gone from the step. Your phone rings once in the night. Nobody speaks.

tip.label: Report an envelope of cash left for an old tenant
tip.reply: Don’t touch it, and don’t answer that phone. An officer will collect it tonight.

envelope.collected: An officer collected the envelope overnight. Doreen says thank you.

news.title: CASH ON DOORSTEP LINKED TO MOTEL GANG
news.summary: A resident handed in an envelope left for a former tenant.
news.body: An envelope of cash, left on a doorstep for a former tenant, has been linked by detectives to a gang working out of the interstate motel.{short}

envelope.newsShort: Police say the money was missing.
deaths: They knew which door it was. They had delivered it.
Nobody heard a thing.
The phone rang once, from somewhere inside the room.

cleaner.hook: I clean three houses up on the ridge. Bluebird houses. You would not believe what rich people leave lying around.
cleaner.clue: {name} steals from the Bluebird houses she cleans on the ridge.

ask.label: Ask what they leave lying around
ask.player: Like what?
ask.reply: Rings. Bracelets. Things nobody has worn in years. Nobody counts. Want a ring? For your future wife. Cheap.

buy.label: Buy a ring from her
buy.reply: Tomorrow, under your mat. Don’t wear it on the ridge.

warn.label: Tell her she’ll get caught
warn.reply: Nobody counts. That’s the whole point of being rich.

cleaner.delivered: A small velvet pouch, pushed under your door. Inside: an old diamond ring, far too good to be cheap.

item.label: A diamond ring (don’t ask)
item.text: An old diamond ring in a velvet pouch, from {first}. Far too good to be cheap.

story.title: HEIRLOOM RING MISSING FROM RIDGE HOME
story.summary: The Ashworth family say a diamond ring has vanished.
story.body: A diamond ring that has been in the Ashworth family for four generations has gone missing from their home on the ridge. Mrs. Constance Ashworth said nobody had worn it in years, but she noticed at once. Police are speaking to domestic staff.

tip.label: Report a cleaner stealing from the ridge houses
tip.reply: The ridge. Right. We’ll have a word with the agency. Thank you, love.

handIn.label: Hand in a ring you were sold
handIn.reply: Hand it in? Good man. Leave it in an envelope by the door and an officer will collect it. Nobody needs to know where it came from.

cleaner.handedNotice: An officer collected the ring. Doreen says the Ashworths will be very glad.

tb.label: Tell her about the Ashworths’ cleaner
tb.player: I think I know who took the Ashworths’ ring. Their cleaner.
tb.reply: The Ashworths’ cleaner? Leave it with me. Constance will be very grateful.

cleaner.thanks: The Ashworths are telling everyone you handed in that ring. Well done, you.

arrested.title: CLEANER CHARGED OVER RIDGE THEFTS
arrested.summary: {name} cleaned three homes on the ridge.
arrested.body: {name}, who cleaned three homes on the ridge, has been charged with theft. Police say they are tracing everything she sold.

cleaner.friend: Did you have something to do with {first} getting arrested?

watch.name: Constance Ashworth
watch.clue: Constance Ashworth chairs the Ridge Neighborhood Watch. She keeps a file on everyone in Sunfall.
watch.open: Constance Ashworth. I chair the Ridge Neighborhood Watch. You’re the young man who is always at home. We have a use for people who are always at home.
watch.openRing: Constance Ashworth. You’re the young man who found my ring. I chair the Ridge Neighborhood Watch, and I have a use for people who are always at home.
watch.what: Information. Who comes and goes. Who says what. Girls talk to you, I gather. I keep a file on everyone in Sunfall. I would like to keep one with you, rather than on you.
watch.joined: Splendid. I’ll have a page from the file put through your door in the morning, so you know where you stand. Then I’ll ring. Have something for me.
watch.refused: How disappointing. You have a window, you know. Everyone does.
watch.ask: Constance Ashworth. Well? Tell me something about one of your girls.
watch.took: How interesting. Thank you. The Bluebirds will hear good things about you.
watch.nothing: Nothing? I do hope that isn’t becoming a habit.
watch.page: A cream envelope through your letterbox, with the Ashworth crest. Inside: one typed page from the Watch file. It’s about you.

pageItem.label: A page from the Watch file
pageItem.text: One typed page under the Ashworth crest: your name, your window, the time your light goes off, and the names of the women you talk to.

watch.betrayed: How does Constance Ashworth know what I told you? I told YOU that. Nobody else. Don’t ever message me again.

column.title: WHAT THE WATCH KNOWS
column.summary: A local woman’s private business, courtesy of an anonymous friend.
column.body: The Ridge Neighborhood Watch notes that {name} has not been entirely honest with the people around her. An anonymous friend tells us more.

watch.window: Constance Ashworth showed me a photograph of you at your window at night. Every night. Explain.

newsroom.label: Tell the newsroom about Constance Ashworth’s files
newsroom.noProof: A neighborhood watch with files on everyone? Get us one page and we’ll run it.
newsroom.proof: One page is all we need. This runs tomorrow.

expose.title: WATCH CHAIR KEPT SECRET FILES ON RESIDENTS
expose.summary: Typed pages seen by the Sunfall Daily list who comes and goes, and when lights go off.
expose.body: Constance Ashworth, chair of the Ridge Neighborhood Watch, kept typed files on hundreds of Sunfall residents, the Sunfall Daily can reveal. Mrs. Ashworth said she was simply being neighborly.

watch.exposedCall: You. Do you know how long I have kept this town in order? Enjoy your window.
watch.tbCool: Did you go to the paper about Constance? Half the club isn’t speaking to the other half.
watch.othersWarm: Was it you who exposed that Ashworth woman? She had a file on my mom. Thank you.

hook.mogger: Darling, confession. I’m at the end of my twelve-seat table, three glasses into a very good red, looking at your photos instead of my soup. I was married twice. Tommy for love, Walter for the house. Neither of them ever looked like you. Would you be my husband tonight? On the telephone. I’ll do all the remembering.
hook.normie: Darling. I’m at the end of my twelve-seat table again with a bottle I promised myself I’d ration. I was married twice: Tommy for love, Walter for the house. Both gone. Some nights I’d give the house to hear Tommy say goodnight again. Would you be him? On the telephone. Just for an evening.
hook.truecel: Don’t read anything into this. I’m at the end of my twelve-seat table, I’m drunk, and you’re the only man on this app who answers at this hour. I was married twice: Tommy for love, Walter for the house. Both gone. I need a man’s voice on the telephone saying Tommy’s things. In the dark you could be anyone. Would you do it?

yes.label: Tell her to ring you tonight
yes.player: Ring me tonight. I’ll be whoever you need.

reply.mogger: Oh, you angel. Tonight, then. My number is {number}, so you know it’s me.
reply.normie: Tonight, then. My number is {number}, so you know it’s me. Don’t laugh at me.
reply.truecel: Fine. Tonight. My number is {number}. Don’t make it weird.

no.label: Tell her it’s too strange
no.player: That’s a bit too strange for me, Diana.

reply.mogger: Of course. Forget I asked. I’m blushing at a soup tureen.
reply.normie: No. You’re right. Forget I asked, darling.
reply.truecel: Fine. I don’t know why I asked you anyway.

said.mogger: It’s me. I’m on the sofa in the small sitting room with the lights off. Here’s how it works. Tommy wrote me letters from every rodeo on the circuit. I’m sending them to you, with his belt buckle and Walter’s robe, because Tommy never owned a robe in his life. Learn him. Then I’ll ring, and you’ll say his things back to me.
said.normie: It’s me. Lights off, sofa, the small sitting room. Here’s how it works. Tommy wrote me letters from every rodeo on the circuit. I’m sending them to you, with his belt buckle and Walter’s robe. Learn him. Then I’ll ring, and you’ll say his things back to me.
said.truecel: It’s me. Lights off, so I can’t see the phone and remember who’s on it. Tommy wrote me letters from every rodeo on the circuit. I’m sending them to you, with his belt buckle and Walter’s robe. Learn him. Don’t improvise. You’re not a natural.

reply.mogger: Tomorrow, then. Wear the robe when I ring. And darling? Nobody has ever learned anything for me.
reply.normie: Tomorrow, then. Wear the robe when I ring.
reply.truecel: Tomorrow, then. Wear the robe. It won’t fit you. Wear it anyway.

hang.mogger: Coward. A lovely coward, but a coward.
hang.normie: You hung up on me. Coward.

parcel.label: Diana’s parcel: a robe, a buckle and letters
parcel.text: A heavy wine-red silk robe with W.H. stitched in gold on the pocket, smelling of cigars and somebody else’s cologne. A tarnished rodeo belt buckle, a bull’s head worn smooth by a thumb. And a bundle of letters in a cowboy’s capitals, tied with a blue ribbon. Every one starts the same way: Evening, Dee. Saddle up. The one from the desert says: The desert keeps no secrets, Dee, but I keep yours. And the last, from the night before the bull: I’d ride a thousand miles of bad road for one more supper at your table.

notice.mogger: It fits like it was cut for you. Walter must have been a big man once. You look like the portrait in a house you could never afford.
notice.normie: It’s tight across the middle and smells of cigars. You tie it anyway. You feel like a man who owns a dam.
notice.truecel: It hangs off your shoulders like a tent on a coat hanger. It smells of cigars and of a man who was everything you aren’t. You tie it twice.

cues.said: Lights off. I’m in the dining room now, at his end of the table. Start the way he always started. Go on.
cues.dirty: Forget the letters. Tell me what you’re wearing at the end of that table.

cues.said: Now the desert one. The one he wrote from the trailer in the dark. What does the desert keep?
cues.right: The desert keeps no secrets, Dee. But I keep yours.
cues.wrong: The desert keeps the heat. Like you do.
cues.dirty: The desert keeps nothing. I want to keep you up all night.

cues.said: The last letter. The night before the bull. Say it the way he said it.
cues.right: I’d ride a thousand miles of bad road for one more supper at your table.
cues.wrong: I’ll always love you, Dee. Always.

mogger: Oh. That’s him. Except he never sounded like that. Again, slower.
Darling, I’ve had to put the glass down. Keep the robe on. Keep talking.
I’m lying on his end of the table and I can’t breathe. Tommy never once made me feel like this. You did it with his words.
normie: That’s him. That’s exactly him. Say it again, slower.
I’ve put the glass down. Keep talking like that. Is the robe on?
I’m on the table. His end. I haven’t felt like this since the bull. Thank you, darling. Goodnight, Tommy.
truecel: That’s him. Don’t talk after you say it. Just breathe.
Better. You sound like him when you don’t sound like you. Keep it like that.
I’m lying on the table in the dark and for a minute you were him. Don’t say anything. Don’t ruin it. Goodnight.

wrong.mogger: No, darling. He’d never say that. You can make it up to me tomorrow.
wrong.normie: He’d never say that. You haven’t read them, have you? Tomorrow.
wrong.truecel: That’s not him. That’s you. I can hear the difference. Tomorrow.

win.mogger: Tommy never had a mouth like yours. Forget Tommy. Say it again, and say it to me.
win.normie: Oh. Tommy never said things like that. Maybe he should have. Again.

lose.mogger: Not yet, darling. Him first. Then you.
