lose.normie: Don’t. That’s not him. Do it properly tomorrow.
lose.truecel: Don’t. You were doing so well when you were him.

picture.mogger: So you know what you did to me.
picture.normie: So you know what Tommy’s words did. Your voice, I mean.
picture.truecel: Don’t show anyone. I mean it.

missedVm.mogger: It’s Diana. I sat at his end of the table for an hour with the robe over the chair. Ring me, darling.
missedVm.normie: It’s Diana. I sat at his end of the table for an hour. Ring me tomorrow.
missedVm.truecel: It’s Diana. You didn’t pick up. Nobody ever does.

celeste.name: Celeste Van Doren

open.mogger: Good evening. This is Celeste Van Doren, from the club. Diana tells me she has found a new husband on the telephone. She says you’re very handsome. The committee does so like to meet a girl’s husbands.
open.normie: Good evening. This is Celeste Van Doren, from the club. Diana tells me she has found a new husband on the telephone. The committee does so like to meet a girl’s husbands.
open.truecel: Good evening. This is Celeste Van Doren, from the club. Diana tells me she has found a new husband on the telephone. I asked to see a picture. She showed me your profile. Oh dear.

player.not: I’m not her husband. We just talk.

available.mogger: Oh, you’ll do beautifully. You’ll have a little something in the post. Welcome to the family.
available.normie: How lovely. The committee will vote. You’ll have a little something in the post either way.
available.truecel: Available. Yes, I imagine you are. The committee doesn’t vote in men like you, dear. It would be cruel to the furniture.

not.mogger: Of course not. Nobody ever is, at first. Goodnight.
not.normie: Of course not. Nobody ever is, at first. Goodnight.
not.truecel: No. I didn’t think so. Goodnight.

celeste.vm: Celeste Van Doren again. Hanging up on a lady is very rude. The committee will remember it.
celeste.missedVm: Good evening. This is Celeste Van Doren, from the club, about Diana. I shall try you again tomorrow.

ribbon.label: A cream envelope with a blue ribbon
ribbon.text: Inside, a length of blue ribbon, the exact blue of the club, and a card in fountain pen: Welcome to the family. No name. No date.

voted.mogger: The committee voted. Darling, they voted yes. I’ve never been so frightened or so happy.
voted.normie: The committee voted. They voted yes. I don’t know whether to kiss you or warn you.

not.mogger: Celeste rang you. I’m sorry. I still want Tommy’s voice tonight. Yours, I mean.
not.normie: Celeste rang you, didn’t she. I’m so sorry. Let’s stop for a while.
not.truecel: You told Celeste you’re not my husband. As if anyone would think you were. Goodnight.

hang.mogger: Did you hang up on Celeste? Nobody hangs up on Celeste. I think I’m in love.
hang.normie: Did you hang up on Celeste? Darling, nobody hangs up on Celeste. Be careful.
hang.truecel: You hung up on Celeste. Now I have to hear about it at lunch for a year. Thanks.

after.joke: Celeste told the whole club. They’re calling you my charity case. Don’t ring me.

deaths: The window was open. You never open the window.
Walter fell too.
There was a blue ribbon tied to your door handle when they found you.

hang.title: WHO HUNG UP ON CELESTE?
hang.summary: The club is agog: a gentleman caller put the phone down on Mrs. Van Doren.
hang.body: Members of the Bluebird Club report that a gentleman, a telephone friend of one of the club’s most generous donors, hung up on Celeste Van Doren this week. Mrs. Van Doren declined to comment, beyond saying that the committee has a long memory.

joke.title: THE CLUB’S LATEST JOKE
joke.summary: A donor’s late-night telephone friend is not, we hear, committee material.
joke.body: Laughter at the Bluebird Club this week over a much-loved donor’s late-night telephone companion, who offered himself to the committee and was told, kindly, that he would be cruel to the furniture.

hook.mogger: Confession: we’re neighbors. Across the landing, above the laundromat. I’ve seen you on the stairs and I’ve thought about it all week. I show rich people’s houses all day. Want to see where I’m not supposed to be?
hook.normie: You know we’re neighbors? Across the landing, above the laundromat. I hear your TV. Anyway. I show rich people’s houses all day and I get bored between viewings. Want to see where I’m not supposed to be?
hook.truecel: So my friends and I have a game. I show rich people’s houses, and between viewings I send pictures from places I shouldn’t be, to someone who’ll appreciate it. They picked you. We’re neighbors, by the way. Across the landing. I’ve heard you through the wall. Want to see?

reply.mogger: First viewing at ten tomorrow. Watch your phone, neighbor.
reply.normie: First viewing at ten tomorrow. Watch your phone.
reply.truecel: First viewing at ten tomorrow. Don’t be gross about it.

reply.mogger: Boring. Gorgeous, but boring.
reply.normie: Boring. Fine.
reply.truecel: Wow. Okay. My friends are going to love that.

spots.island: Show home on Mesa Vista. The buyers are in the garden arguing about a pool. I’m on their kitchen island.
spots.bed: Their bed. Eight hundred thread count and a husband who sleeps on the left. I’m on the left.
spots.tub: Their bathtub. Clawfoot, original features. The buyers are downstairs measuring the curtains.
spots.closet: Her closet. Her silk robe. She has nineteen of them. She won’t miss one for ten minutes.
spots.master: Last one. A big house on the ridge road, the old judge’s place. The owner is some tennis woman who never smiles. Her master bedroom. Her sheets.

mogger: My heart is going. That’s you, not the house. Where next, neighbor?
Still shaking. In a good way. Pick the next one, neighbor.
That was the best ten minutes of my week. Where to now?
normie: Your turn. Where next?
Okay, that was fun. Pick the next house.
I can’t stop grinning. Where next?
truecel: My friends are screaming. Where next?
Okay, I’m telling everyone about that one. Next?
That was insane. Pick another one before I lose my nerve.

masterAfter.mogger: Okay. That one felt like being watched. Later, neighbor.
masterAfter.normie: Okay. That one felt like being watched. Later.
masterAfter.truecel: That house was creepy. Felt like being watched. Bye.

caroline.name: Caroline Prescott

open.mogger: This is Caroline Prescott. You don’t know me. You know my bed. I have cameras in every room of my father’s house, because of the kind of people I’m building a case against, and yesterday they watched a realtor photograph herself on my sheets and send it to you. I’ve left you a still. Then I looked at your profile. Twice.
open.normie: This is Caroline Prescott. You don’t know me. You know my bed. I have cameras in every room of my father’s house, because of the kind of people I’m building a case against, and yesterday they watched a realtor photograph herself on my sheets and send it to you. I’ve left you a still. I want to know what the fuss is about.
open.truecel: This is Caroline Prescott. You don’t know me. You know my bed. I have cameras in every room of my father’s house, because of the kind of people I’m building a case against, and yesterday they watched a realtor photograph herself on my sheets and send it to you. I’ve left you a still. I looked at your profile. I want to know what she was laughing about.

player.sorry: I’m sorry. I didn’t know it was your house.

what.mogger: A rematch. She sent you my bed from the edge of it. I’ll send you my bed from the middle. Then you choose. I always win.
what.normie: A rematch. She used my house to impress you. I’ll show you how it’s done properly. Then you choose.
what.truecel: I want her to lose something. You’re what she was playing with. So I’ll play with it better.

caroline.sorry: Don’t apologize. Compete. I’ll be in your phone tomorrow.
caroline.vm: You hung up on me. Nobody hangs up on me. Check your floor, then check your phone.

still.label: A security camera still
still.text: A grainy black-and-white print from a camera high in the corner of a big bedroom: Olivia Reid on the bed, phone held up, mid-laugh, a time stamp in the corner. On the back, in hard capitals: SHE LOSES. C.P.

bed.mogger: My bed, from the middle. Now you know the difference.
bed.normie: My bed, from the middle. Now you know the difference.
bed.truecel: My bed, from the middle. Look as long as you like. That’s all you get to do.

court.mogger: My court. I play against the wall because nobody else will play me. Play me.
court.normie: My court. I play against the wall because nobody else will play me. Your move.
court.truecel: My court. I play against the wall. The wall has more going for it than you. Choose anyway.

heard.mogger: Someone called my office about a house on the ridge road. She called you too? I’m the better view and you know it.
heard.normie: Someone called my office about a house on the ridge road. I think I’m in trouble. Did she call you?
heard.truecel: Someone called my office about the ridge road house. Did you tell on me? My friends say you did.

olivia.label: Tell Olivia it’s her
olivia.player: It’s you, Olivia. It was always going to be you.

olivia.mogger: Neighbor. I’m going to knock on your wall three times tonight. Knock back.
olivia.normie: Me? Okay. I’m smiling at a wall. It’s your wall, technically.
olivia.truecel: Wait, you actually picked me? That’s sweet. My friends are crying. No, obviously.

caroline.mogger: Of course. I always win. Stay on the phone with me tonight. I’ve never had anyone to beat.
caroline.normie: Of course I win. I always win. It’s nicer than usual.
caroline.truecel: You chose me. Good. That’s all I needed: her to lose. We’re done.

olivia.mogger: Seriously? Her? Fine. I’m telling the whole ridge road about her bed.
olivia.normie: Her? Fine. Then everyone gets to hear about her bed.
olivia.truecel: You chose her? Over me? I was never going to choose you either. Bye.

caroline.mogger: Second place. I’ve never been second. I hate how interesting that is. She still loses her job.
caroline.normie: Fine. Second place. She still loses her job.
caroline.truecel: Of course you chose her. She still loses her job, and I still never think about you again.

fired.mogger: I got fired. A client’s camera. Worth it. Mostly.
fired.normie: I got fired. A client’s camera. Was I worth it?

fired.title: REALTOR LET GO AFTER PRIVATE VIEWING
fired.summary: A Sunfall agency parts ways with an agent after footage from a ridge road house.
fired.body: A Sunfall realty agency has let an agent go after a homeowner on the ridge road produced security footage of her photographing herself in the master bedroom during a viewing. The homeowner said she had installed cameras for reasons of her own and was glad she had.

ridge.title: THE JUDGE’S HOUSE, SHOWN IN PERSON
ridge.summary: Buyers say the owner of the old Prescott house gives very personal tours.
ridge.body: Prospective buyers of the late Judge Prescott’s house on the ridge road report that the master bedroom is the most talked about room in Sunfall this month. The owner, a keen tennis player, did not return calls.

hotline.title: 1-900-SUNFALL

ad.title: SUNFALL AFTER DARK
ad.summary: Lonely? Real local girls, live on the line, all night.
ad.body: Real local girls who want to hear from you. Live, discreet, all night long. Call {number}. Four ninety-nine a minute. Adults only. Ask for Candy.

greeting.mogger: Hi, you’ve reached Sunfall After Dark, this is Candy. Oh. Your voice is nice. That’s not in the script. Sorry. What would you like to hear?
greeting.normie: Hi, you’ve reached Sunfall After Dark, this is Candy. I’m, um, lying on a satin bed. Allegedly. What would you like to hear?
greeting.truecel: Sunfall After Dark, this is Candy. You’re being charged four ninety-nine a minute. What do you want to hear?

hotline.busy: Candy is with another caller tonight. Try tomorrow, handsome. That’s the recording. It says handsome to everyone.

topics.label: Ask what she’s wearing

reply.mogger: A red slip, and nothing under it, and I’m. Wow, I lost my place. Sorry. I’ve got ointment on my hands, I was doing inventory. Ignore that. The slip. Red.
reply.normie: A little red slip, and nothing underneath, and I’m thinking about you. Hold on, I lost the page. Sorry, I have hydrocortisone on my hands from work. Never mind. Red. Slip.
reply.truecel: Red slip. Nothing underneath. Thinking about you. That’s the script. I’m reading it off a page next to a box of hemorrhoid cream, so let’s not pretend.

topics.clue: Candy on Sunfall After Dark had ointment on her hands from work. Inventory.

topics.label: Ask her to tell you a secret
topics.player: Tell me a secret, Candy. A real one.

reply.mogger: A real one? I sing second soprano in a church choir and I’ve mouthed the high notes for four years. Oh no. That’s real. Pretend I said something about a hot tub. Actually, don’t. I liked telling you.
reply.normie: A secret. Okay. I sing second soprano in a church choir and I’ve been mouthing the high notes for four years. Oh no. That’s a real one. Pretend I said something about a hot tub.
reply.truecel: A secret. I sing in a church choir and mouth the high notes. There. That’s the only secret you’re getting for four ninety-nine.

topics.clue: Candy on Sunfall After Dark sings second soprano in a church choir and mouths the high notes.

topics.label: Ask why she does this
topics.player: Why do you do this, Candy?

reply.mogger: Because it’s a script. I rehearse everything, even phone calls, out loud in the shower. Here the script never runs out and nobody sees my face go red. And it pays for a course I can’t afford. You’re the first caller I’ve wanted to go off script for.
reply.normie: Because it’s a script. I rehearse everything, even phone calls, out loud in the shower. Here the script never runs out and nobody sees my face go red. And it pays for a course I can’t afford.
reply.truecel: Because it’s a script. I rehearse phone calls in the shower and here the script never runs out, and nobody I know would ever call this line. Right?

topics.clue: Candy on Sunfall After Dark rehearses phone calls out loud in the shower.

name.label: Ask her real name
name.reply: Candy. It says so in the paper. Well, it doesn’t. But it’s Candy.

know.label: Tell her you know she’s Jessica
know.player: Ointment, the choir, the shower. You’re Jessica Rivera.

yes.mogger: Oh my God. You. It’s you? I’ve been reading this script to you and pretending you were nobody. Hang up. Text me on Hinge. I want to say all of it again without the page.
yes.normie: Nobody can know. Not even you. Okay. You know. I’m going to hang up and die in the shower. Then text me.

no.normie: No. No, no. You can’t know that. I’m hanging up. Please never call this number again.
no.truecel: Not you. Anyone but you. I’m hanging up. Please never call this number again.

yes.mogger: No script this time. I’m still at the counter after closing. Here.
yes.normie: Okay. No script. I rehearsed this text forty times. Here.

no.truecel: Please don’t ever message me. Please.

goodbye.mogger: You’re my favorite caller. I’m not supposed to say that. I’m quitting tomorrow. Don’t tell anyone.
goodbye.normie: Same time tomorrow? No. I’m quitting. I think I just wanted someone to hear me say things.
goodbye.truecel: You called three nights in a row. Do you know what that says about you? Don’t answer. That was my last shift.

hotline.closed: The number you have dialed is no longer in service.

bill.label: Your phone bill
bill.text: Sunfall After Dark, forty-one minutes at four ninety-nine a minute. You read it twice. It doesn’t get smaller.

spotter.title: Spotter

hook.normie: I looked at your photos. Can I be honest? That little belly. You’re soft. I like soft things I can boss around. I’m a trainer. I could train you. Or I could punish you. With me it’s the same thing.
hook.mogger: I looked at your photos. Pretty boy. I bet nobody has ever told you what to do in your whole life. I want to. I’m a trainer. I could train you. Or I could punish you. With me it’s the same thing.
hook.truecel: I looked at your photos. The cans on the desk behind you. The pizza box. You live like a pig in a sty. I’m a trainer. I could fix you. Or I could just enjoy you. With me it’s the same thing.

reply.normie: Rules. Three mornings. I ring early. You answer, or you ring me straight back. You call me Coach. My number is {number}. Good piggy.
reply.mogger: Rules. Three mornings. I ring early. You answer, or you ring me straight back. You call me Coach. My number is {number}. Good boy. Piggy.
reply.truecel: Rules. Three mornings. I ring early. You answer, or you ring me straight back. You call me Coach. My number is {number}. Clean that desk, piggy.

reply.normie: Your loss. I was going to be so mean to you.
reply.mogger: Your loss, pretty boy. I was going to be so mean to you.
reply.truecel: Your loss. Enjoy your sty.

parcel.label: Lauren’s box: a pull-up bar and a pig nose
parcel.text: A long box. A door-frame pull-up bar, a rubber pig nose on an elastic band, and a note in thick marker: WEAR THE NOSE. FIT THE BAR. DAY THREE. COACH.

notice.normie: You put it on. You catch yourself in the dark window. You make a noise you didn’t know you could make.
notice.mogger: You put it on. Even like this you’re annoyingly handsome. That’s probably the point.
notice.truecel: You put it on. It fits. That’s the worst part.

bar.label: 🔩 Fit the bar to the door frame
bar.notice: It takes twenty minutes and most of your patience. It holds when you hang off it. Mostly.

open.normie: You picked up. Good piggy. Floor. Hands under your shoulders. Ten push-ups on my count, and every time you go down, you say thank you, Coach.
open.mogger: Look at you, picking up like a good boy. Floor. Ten push-ups on my count. Pretty boys hate this part. That’s why I love it.
open.truecel: You picked up. Of course you did, you don’t sleep. Floor. Push the cans out of the way. Ten on my count, piggy.

rang.normie: Floor. Hands under your shoulders. Ten push-ups on my count, and every time you go down, you say thank you, Coach.
rang.mogger: Floor, pretty boy. Ten push-ups on my count. Pretty boys hate this part. That’s why I love it.
rang.truecel: Floor. Push the cans out of the way. Ten on my count, piggy.

open.normie: Day two. Are you wearing the nose? Don’t tell me. Oink if you are. Fifteen today. Faster.
open.mogger: Day two. My class this morning was twelve women and none of them were as much fun as you. Fifteen. Faster.
open.truecel: Day two. I broke a girl’s nose sparring once. Don’t make me miss you. Fifteen.

open.normie: Day three. Is the bar up? Then hang off it. Five pull-ups. Every one, you tell me what you are.
open.mogger: Day three. The bar. Five pull-ups, pretty boy, and you thank me for every one.
open.truecel: Day three. The bar. Five pull-ups. I don’t think you can do one. Prove me wrong, piggy.

sessions.noBar: You didn’t fit the bar? Floor, then. Ten burpees, and you’ll think about why you disobeyed me.

hangText.normie: You hung up on me. You don’t get to waste me, piggy. Tomorrow you do double.
hangText.mogger: You hung up on me. Nobody hangs up on me, pretty boy. Tomorrow you pay for it.
hangText.truecel: You hung up on me. In your sty. Tomorrow.

spotter.quit: Twice. We’re done. I don’t train quitters.

missedVm.normie: Coach here. You didn’t pick up. Ring me back today, piggy, or it counts as a miss.
missedVm.mogger: Coach here. You didn’t pick up, pretty boy. Ring me back today or it costs you.
missedVm.truecel: Coach. You didn’t pick up. Probably asleep in the crumbs. Ring me back today or it counts.

scene.push: On the floor by the bed, the phone on speaker by your face. Tap on her count.
scene.pull: Hanging off the bar in the door frame, the phone on speaker on the floor below. Tap on her count.

normie: One. Good piggy.
Two. Feel that belly touch the floor?
Three. Say thank you, Coach.
Four. Dirty little piggy.
Five. You’re sweating already. Disgusting. Keep going.
Six. I can hear you wheezing. I love it.
Seven. Lower.
Eight. Who owns you this morning?
Nine. Almost, piggy.
Ten. Stay down there. I like you down there.
Eleven. Oink for me.
Twelve. Filthy.
Thirteen. I’m not even tired. You are.
Fourteen. Beg for the last one.
Fifteen. Good piggy.
mogger: One. Pretty boy.
Two. Not so pretty now.
Three. Thank me.
Four. Dirty little piggy. Even you.
Five. Nobody’s ever made you sweat for it, have they?
Six. Lower, gorgeous.
Seven. I could do this all day.
Eight. Say it. Thank you, Coach.
Nine. That face, ruined. Perfect.
Ten. Stay there. Look at you.
Eleven. Oink, pretty boy.
Twelve. I’d frame this.
Thirteen. All those girls who think you’re perfect.
Fourteen. Beg.
Fifteen. Good boy. Good piggy.
truecel: One. Piggy.
Two. Your arms are shaking already.
Three. Thank me.
Four. Dirty little piggy in your little sty.
Five. When did you last see sunlight?
Six. Lower. Into the crumbs.
Seven. I can hear the cans rolling.
Eight. Who owns you?
Nine. Pathetic. Don’t stop.
Ten. Stay down there. It suits you.
Eleven. Oink.
Twelve. You’re not even fat. You’re just filthy.
Thirteen. Nobody else would bother with you.
Fourteen. Beg.
Fifteen. Good. Piggy.

normie: Too slow, piggy. That one doesn’t count.
Did I say stop? Again.
Lazy. You’ll pay for that.
mogger: Too slow, pretty boy.
Did I say stop? Again.
Lazy. Even beautiful things get punished.
truecel: Too slow, piggy.
Did I say stop? Again.
Lazy. Like everything else about you.

spotter.fail: Three misses. Pathetic. Get up. Same time tomorrow, and you’ll beg for it.

normie: Ten. Good piggy. I’m breathing harder than you are and I didn’t do anything. Same time tomorrow.
Fifteen. Look what you did. I had to sit down. Tomorrow, the bar.
Five. Good piggy. My good piggy. I’m going to think about that noise you made all day.
mogger: Ten. Look at you, flushed. I want a picture of your face right now and I’d never show anyone.
Fifteen. I had to put the phone face down so I could hear you breathe. Tomorrow, the bar.
Five. Pretty boy, ruined, and thanking me for it. That’s the best thing anyone has ever given me.
truecel: Ten. You did it. I hate how much I liked listening to that.
Fifteen. Disgusting. Again tomorrow. I mean it. I want it.
Five. You know why I do this? I tell women all day they’re fine as they are, and I go home and hate my thighs. You’re where I get to put it. Same time next week, piggy.

whistle.normie: So you remember who you answer to.
whistle.mogger: So you remember who you answer to, pretty boy.
whistle.truecel: Look. Don’t touch. Not that you could.

bench.mogger: You earned one. Don’t get used to it.

pitch.normie: You rang me? Brave. I’ve seen your photos. That little belly. I’m a trainer. I could train you, or I could punish you, and with me it’s the same thing. Want in?
pitch.mogger: You rang me first? Pretty boy. I bet nobody has ever told you what to do. I’m a trainer. I could train you, or I could punish you, and with me it’s the same thing. Want in?
pitch.truecel: You rang me? From the sty? Okay. I’m a trainer. I could fix you, or I could just enjoy you, and with me it’s the same thing. Want in?

yes.normie: Rules. Three mornings. I ring early. You answer, or you ring me straight back. You call me Coach. Good piggy.
yes.mogger: Rules. Three mornings. I ring early. You answer, or you ring me straight back. You call me Coach. Good boy. Piggy.
yes.truecel: Rules. Three mornings. I ring early. You answer, or you ring me straight back. You call me Coach. Clean that desk, piggy.

self.normie: You rang me first. Eager little piggy. I like eager.
self.mogger: You rang me first. Nobody rings me first, pretty boy. I like it.
self.truecel: You rang me first. Couldn’t sleep in the crumbs? Fine.

back.normie: Oh, now you ring. I rang you this morning, piggy. You made me wait, so it’s faster today.
back.mogger: Oh, now you ring. You made me wait, pretty boy. Nobody makes me wait. Faster today.
back.truecel: Oh, now you ring. Too busy in the sty to pick up? Faster today.

ring.early: Not yet. I ring you, early, when it’s time. Eat something green and go to sleep, piggy.
ring.doneToday: You already did today. Greedy piggy. Rest. Tomorrow.
ring.failedToday: You already let me down once today. Tomorrow, early. Sleep.
ring.hungUp: You hung up on me this morning. You don’t get to ring me now. Tomorrow.

reply.normie: Oh my God. You’re wearing it. Okay. I’ll go slow for that. My good piggy.
reply.mogger: You’re wearing it. A pretty boy in a pig nose. I’ll go easy for that, and only that.
reply.truecel: You’re actually wearing it. That was the best noise anyone has made at me all year. Slow today.

reply.normie: Make you? Okay. Faster, then. And you’ll thank me for every one.
reply.mogger: Make you? Oh, I was hoping you’d say that. Faster, pretty boy.
reply.truecel: Make you? From the floor of your sty? Faster. Now.

beg.label: Beg her to go easy
beg.player: Please, Coach. Go easy on me today.

easy.normie: Since you asked so nicely. Fewer today. Don’t get used to it.
easy.mogger: Begging suits you. Fewer today, pretty boy.
easy.truecel: Fine. Fewer. You sounded like you meant it.

hard.mogger: Begging? You? That’s faster, pretty boy.
hard.truecel: Begging gets you nothing in here. Faster.

talk.label: Ask about her
player: Can I ask you something, Coach? Why this?
Who taught you to be like this, Lauren?
Who trains you, Coach?
reply: I danced for nine years. Every week somebody with a clipboard told me what was wrong with my body. Now I’m the one holding the stopwatch. It’s nicer on this side.
Six years with a man who weighed my dinner plate. I never said a word. The first time I told you to drop, it was the first time in my life I was the one saying it.
Nobody. I tell women all day they’re fine as they are. Then I go home and pinch my thighs in the mirror. You’re where I get to put it. Don’t make it weird.

pretty.label: Tell her she’s beautiful
pretty.player: You’re beautiful, Lauren. Thighs and all.

reply.normie: Stop it. No. Okay. Say it again tomorrow.
reply.mogger: Coming from you, that almost counts. Almost. Say it again.
reply.truecel: You’d say that to anyone who rang you. No. You wouldn’t, would you. Thank you.

turn.label: Tell her it’s your turn to count

reply.normie: You count for me? Nobody ever has. Fine. Tomorrow, I ring you. Don’t be nice to me. I’ll know if you’re lying.
reply.mogger: You, counting for me? Bossy. I didn’t know you had it in you. Tomorrow. I ring you.
reply.truecel: You want to count for me. From your bed. Okay. Tomorrow. If you laugh at me I’ll know.

quiet.label: Say nothing
quiet.reply: Good. Don’t make it a thing. Same time next week, piggy.

open.normie: You said you’d count for me. So count. Squats. Ten. The phone’s on the gym floor and I’m right over it. Count me down, and mean it.
open.mogger: Okay, bossy. Squats. Ten. The phone’s on the gym floor and I’m right over it. Count me down.
open.truecel: You said you’d count. Squats. Ten. The phone’s on the floor and I’m right over it. Count, and don’t laugh.

turn.scene: On your bed, the phone on speaker on your chest. Across town she’s over her own phone on a gym floor. Tap on her breath.
count: Four. I can hear you smiling.
Five. Halfway. Don’t you dare stop.
Six. Your thighs are fine. Six.
Seven. Who owns you this morning?
Nine. Beg for the last one.
miss: Did you skip one? That one doesn’t count. Again.
Keep up. I’m doing all the work here.
turn.fail: You can’t even count. Tomorrow, then. I’m keeping score now.

done.normie: Ten. I’m on the floor. Nobody has ever counted for me. Okay. I need a minute. Thank you, piggy. Thank you.
done.mogger: Ten. I’m flat on the floor and laughing. Nobody has ever counted for me, pretty boy. Thank you.
done.truecel: Ten. I’m on the floor. You meant every one of them. I could hear it. Nobody has ever done that for me.

turn.hang: You said you would. Never mind. Forget I said anything.
turn.missedVm: You were going to count for me. I waited on the gym floor like an idiot. Ring me if you still want to.

picture.normie: Proof. Look what you did to me.
picture.mogger: Proof. Don’t show anyone. Especially not the pretty girls.
picture.truecel: Proof. I never send these. Delete it. Don’t delete it.

ask.normie: One more thing. Send me your address. You’re getting a box from me, and you’ll do what’s in it.
ask.mogger: One more thing, pretty boy. Send me your address. You’re getting a box from me, and you’ll do what’s in it.
ask.truecel: One more thing. Your address. You’re getting a box from me. Clear a space in the sty for it.

give.label: Give her your address
give.player: Here’s my address. What’s in the box?

reply.normie: You’ll see. It’ll be at your door in the morning.
reply.mogger: You’ll see, pretty boy. Your door, in the morning.
reply.truecel: You’ll see. Your door, in the morning. Try not to eat it.

no.label: Tell her not to send anything
no.player: Don’t send anything. I’ll manage with what I’ve got.

reply.normie: With what you’ve got. Okay. Floor and burpees, then. No toys for you.
reply.mogger: Fine, pretty boy. Floor only. No toys for you.
reply.truecel: With what you’ve got. Crumbs and a floor. Fine.

arrived.normie: My box is at your door. Open it. Wear the nose. Fit the bar.
arrived.mogger: My box is at your door, pretty boy. Open it. You know what to do.
arrived.truecel: My box is at your door. Pick it up before you trip over it.

deaths: The door frame was older than the building.
She was still counting when the line went quiet.
Five was always going to be one too many.

seating.title: The Seating Plan

hook.normie: I’m going to be direct, because I always am. I arrange people. Who sits beside whom at every dinner this club gives, and who leaves with whom. I’ve been watching your matches, and I want to arrange you. Every morning I choose one of your women and write the first thing you say to her. You send it word for word. Interested?
hook.mogger: Pretty, popular, and nobody has ever once told you what to say. I arrange people. Who sits where, who leaves with whom. I want to arrange you. Every morning I pick one of your women and write your opening line, and you send it, word for word. You’ll hate it. Say yes.
hook.truecel: Nobody has ever written your lines for you. That’s obvious from your profile. I arrange people, more or less for a living. Every morning I’d pick one of your matches and write what you say to her, and you send it word for word. It can’t go worse than your own material. Yes?

reply.normie: Rules. Three mornings. A card under your door, her name on the front and your line on the back. You send it word for word, no edits, no little faces. I’ll know. If it’s ever too much, say the safeword, centerpiece, and I stop, every time. Tomorrow, then.
reply.mogger: Rules. Three mornings. A card under your door, her name on the front and your line on the back. You send it word for word, no edits. I’ll know. If it’s ever too much, say the safeword, centerpiece, and I stop, every time. Good boy.
reply.truecel: Rules. Three mornings. A card under your door, her name on the front and your line on the back. You send it word for word, no edits. I’ll know. If it’s ever too much, say the safeword, centerpiece, and I stop, every time. Try not to embarrass me. Actually, do. That’s the point.

no.label: Tell her no thanks
no.player: I’ll write my own lines, thanks.

reply.normie: Of course you will. I’ve read them. Good luck.
reply.mogger: Pity. You’d have looked lovely humiliated.
reply.truecel: Bold, given the material. Never mind.

parcel.label: Alice’s parcel: a little gilt chair
parcel.text: A gilt ballroom chair the size of your palm, red velvet seat, the kind that holds the place cards at every dinner the club gives. A card tied to it with black ribbon in her hand: PROP MY CARDS IN THIS WHEN YOU SEND THEM. I SEAT EVERYONE. A.B.

sit.label: 🪑 Prop her card in the little chair

notice.normie: You stand it under your lamp and slot her card in. A tiny gilt throne for one line of text. You feel seated.
notice.mogger: Gilt and red velvet, two inches tall, under your lamp. It doesn’t feel like a throne. It feels like a place card.
notice.truecel: The nicest thing in your room is two inches tall, and it isn’t yours. You prop her card in it.

card.label: Alice’s place card: {first}
card.text: Heavy cream card, gilt edge, her handwriting. On the front: {first}. On the back: {line}

morning.normie: Card one is under your door. You’re seated beside {first}. Read it to her word for word. No edits. I’ll know.
morning.mogger: Card one is under your door, pretty boy. You’re seated beside {first}. Word for word. I’ll know.
morning.truecel: Card one is under your door. {first} gets you today. Poor thing. Word for word. I’ll know.

morning.normie: Card two. {first} today. This one is worse. Sit up straight.
morning.mogger: Card two. {first}. This one will cost you, pretty boy. Sit up straight.
morning.truecel: Card two. {first}. This one is worse, which, for you, is quite something.

morning.normie: The last card. {first}. I saved the best one for her. Word for word, darling.
morning.mogger: The last card. {first}. I saved the best one for you, pretty boy.
morning.truecel: The last card. {first}. I saved the best one. Brace.

none: You have nobody worth seating. Match someone, darling, and I’ll seat you tomorrow.
Still an empty chair beside you. Find someone worth the card, darling. Tomorrow.
seating.noneQuit: Still nobody. I can’t seat an empty table. Come back when you have a life.
lines: Before this goes anywhere,
you should know
I practice kissing
on the back of my hand,
and the hand is not impressed.
I should be honest.
I’m very small,
very eager,
and I’m always finished
before the song is.
A woman chooses where I sit,
what I say,
and who I say it to.
I do as I’m told.
Today she chose you.

scene.desk: At your desk, Alice’s card propped against the lamp and {first}’s chat open. Tap her words in the order she wrote them.
scene.chair: At your desk, Alice’s card propped in her little gilt chair under the lamp and {first}’s chat open. Tap her words in the order she wrote them.

seating.hint: Word for word. Tap them in order.

sent.sloppy: Sent. That was not word for word.

react.into: The back of your hand. Okay. Tomorrow you practice on mine, and I tell you everything you’re doing wrong.
react.laugh: I just snorted coffee onto my phone. The hand is not impressed. I’m going to think about that all day.
react.cold: Okay. I’m going to need a minute. Possibly several years.
react.garbled: Are you okay? Those were all the right words in a frightening order.

react.into: Small, eager and quick. Honestly? I could do a lot with that. You’d have to ask very nicely.
react.laugh: Before the song is. I’m crying. Which song? I need to know which song.
react.cold: Why would you tell me that. Why would anyone tell anyone that.
react.garbled: I read that four times. I think you just confessed to something, but I can’t tell what.

react.into: Someone chooses what you say. Oh, I like that very much.
react.laugh: I’m sorry, what? You have a handler?
react.cold: That is the creepiest thing a man has ever sent me, and I once dated a taxidermist.
react.garbled: I don’t know who chose me, but she’d be disappointed in the delivery.

seating.block: Blocking you. Nothing personal. Actually, very personal.

ask: Wait. That isn’t how you talk. That’s Alice Beaumont. She seats people. She did this to my cousin at a wedding. Did Alice put you up to this?
Hang on. A gilt-edged card, word for word? That’s Alice Beaumont’s game. Half the club has had one. Did she make you send that?
I know that phrasing. That’s an Alice Beaumont card. She made my ex read one out at the summer dinner. Was it her?
found.who: Who is she? Who chose me? Tell me her name.

admit.label: Tell her Alice made you
admit.player: It was Alice Beaumont. She makes me send them, word for word.
admit.join: Alice. Of course it was. Tell her I want to write the next one. I have ideas. Most of them are about you.
admit.pity: Oh, you poor thing. She does this. I’m not angry with you. I am going to ring her, though.

deny.label: Say it was all you
deny.player: Nobody made me. That was all me.
deny.reply: All you. Wow. Okay. I’m sending this to the group chat, for science.

join.normie: She came to me. She wants to write one of your cards. I’ve never shared my pen with anyone. I said yes before I could stop myself.
join.mogger: She came to me, pretty boy. She wants a pen too. I’ve never shared one. I’m considering it, which is new.
join.truecel: She came to me wanting a pen. For you. I have no idea what you did, but I’m impressed.

pity.normie: She rang me and called me a monster. Twenty minutes. I lay on the chaise and listened to every word. Best phone call of my year.
pity.mogger: She rang me to call me a monster, on your behalf. You inspire loyalty, pretty boy. Irritating.
pity.truecel: She rang me to call me a monster for what I did to you. Somebody defended you. Write that down somewhere.

deny.normie: You kept my name out of it. Loyal. Wrong, but loyal. The whole club is reading your opener now, by the way.
deny.mogger: You kept my name out of it, pretty boy. Now everyone thinks you wrote it. Delicious.
deny.truecel: You told her you wrote it yourself. She believed you, which says everything. The club is passing it round.

news.title: Sunfall’s Strangest Opener
news.summary: A man is sending women lines nobody would write for themselves.
news.body: The club’s younger members are passing round screenshots of a dating app conversation that opens with a confession nobody asked for. The sender insists he wrote it himself. Nobody believes him. One committee member, asked whether she recognized the style, smiled and said she couldn’t possibly comment.

perfect.normie: Word for word. She read it twice. Don’t ask how I know. Good boy.
perfect.mogger: Word for word, pretty boy. I could feel her face from across town.
perfect.truecel: Word for word. I genuinely didn’t think you’d manage it. Gold star.

sloppy.normie: That was not word for word. I can always tell. A card is a promise, darling, and you mumbled mine.
sloppy.mogger: That was not word for word. Pretty doesn’t cover a mumble.
sloppy.truecel: That was not word for word. You couldn’t even humiliate yourself properly.

seating.missed: You never read her my card. She’s still sitting there, waiting for a line that never came. Once more and I stop seating you.
seating.quit: Twice. I don’t seat men who won’t sit where they’re put. Off you go.

end.normie: Three cards. Three women who will never look at you the same way. You were my favorite table this year.
end.mogger: Three cards, pretty boy. Three women who used to think you were perfect. My favorite table this year.
end.truecel: Three cards. You did every one. Nobody has ever done everything I said. My favorite table this year.

door.normie: The ballroom door at the end of the night. This is where I watch from. Now you know.
door.mogger: Where I watch from. Now you know where to find me, pretty boy.
door.truecel: Where I watch from. Don’t get ideas. Get some ideas.

table.normie: My seating plan for the summer dinner. Look who’s beside me.
table.mogger: My summer dinner. Look who’s beside me. Don’t let it go to your head.
table.truecel: My summer dinner. Look who’s beside me. Nobody is more surprised than I am.

luncheon.normie: Proof. The card, the luncheon, my face. Don’t show anyone. Show everyone.
luncheon.mogger: Proof. Look at my face. You did that, pretty boy.
luncheon.truecel: Proof. My face. Twelve women saw it. You did that from your bedroom.

seating.safe: Centerpiece. Then we stop, right now, and nobody gets a card. You did exactly right saying it. I mean that. I’ll still seat you somewhere nice one day.

talk.label: Ask about her
player: Why do you do this, Alice?
Do you ever join in?
Who seats you, Alice?
reply: Honoria Blackwood seated this club for twenty years, and I carried her place cards. The night she took ill, I picked up her pen and found out it’s the only thing in that building with any power. I haven’t put it down since.
Never. I stand at the ballroom door at the end of the night and watch the pairs leave. That’s mine. The moment two people work out that somebody else chose this for them, and go anyway.
Nobody. Nobody would dare. I’ve sat at the head of every table since Honoria took ill. I always know exactly where I’m sitting. Do you have any idea how tired that makes a person?

seat.label: Tell her you’ll write her card
seat.player: Then I write yours. One card. You read it out loud wherever I put you.

reply.normie: You? Write mine? Nobody has ever. Fine. One card. I’ll read it at the committee luncheon, out loud, in front of all of them. Write it now, before I change my mind.
reply.mogger: Bossy. I didn’t know pretty boys could hold a pen. Fine. One card. I read it at the committee luncheon, out loud. Write it now.
reply.truecel: You want to write me a card. Okay. One. I’ll read it at the committee luncheon in front of every woman who matters in this town. Write it now, before I come to my senses.

kind.label: Tell her that sounds lonely
kind.reply: It is. Don’t you dare be kind to me about it. Tomorrow, darling.

quiet.label: Say nothing
quiet.reply: Good. We don’t discuss it. Tomorrow, darling.

crush.label: Her card: she has a crush
crush.line: Ladies, I have been asked to tell you that I have a crush, that he made me say so, and that I am blushing.

charge.label: Her card: she isn’t in charge
charge.line: I am not in charge of anything today. A man none of you have met chose where I sit and what I say, and I am letting him.

wine.label: Her card: it isn’t the wine
wine.line: I have been instructed to tell the committee that I am very warm, and that it is not the wine.

wrote.normie: Done. Tomorrow, at the luncheon. I’ll ring you from the table so you hear every word. I hate you a little.
wrote.mogger: Done. Tomorrow, at the luncheon, pretty boy. I’ll ring you from the table. I hate you a little.
wrote.truecel: Done. Tomorrow, at the luncheon. I’ll ring you from the table. If you laugh, I’ll know.

open.normie: It’s me. I’m at the luncheon. The phone is face up by my water glass and twelve women are looking at me. I’m standing up. Here it is. {line} They’re staring. Say something.
open.mogger: It’s me. The luncheon. Phone by my glass, twelve women watching. I’m standing. {line} There. Say something, pretty boy.
open.truecel: It’s me. The luncheon. Twelve women, one phone, and your card. I’m standing. {line} Nobody is breathing. Say something.

well.normie: They clapped. Celeste Van Doren clapped. I’ve sat down and my face is on fire. Nobody has ever put me anywhere. Thank you.
well.mogger: They clapped, pretty boy. Celeste Van Doren clapped. My face is on fire. Thank you.
well.truecel: They clapped. For me, for your card. My face is on fire. You did that from your bedroom. Thank you.

again.normie: Again? In front of. Fine. I’m standing back up. {line} There. Celeste has dropped her fork. I have never been so seen in my life. I need to lie down.
again.mogger: Again. You’re cruel. I love it. Standing. {line} Celeste has dropped her fork. I need to lie down.
again.truecel: Again? Okay. Standing. {line} Celeste has dropped her fork. Nobody has ever made me do anything twice. I need to lie down.

turn.hang: You hung up. I read your card to twelve women and you hung up on me. Fine. Lesson learned.
turn.missedVm: I read your card at the luncheon and you didn’t pick up. I read it to a ringing phone. Ring me if you still care.

ask.normie: One more thing. Every man I seat gets a seat. Give me your address and I’ll send you one of the club’s little chairs.
ask.mogger: One more thing, pretty boy. Every man I seat gets a seat. Your address, and I’ll send one of the club’s little chairs.
ask.truecel: One more thing. Every man I seat gets a seat, even you. Your address, and I’ll send one of the club’s little chairs.

give.label: Give her your address
give.player: Here’s my address. A little chair?

reply.normie: A gilt one, the kind that holds the place cards at our dinners. It comes with your first card in the morning. Prop my cards in it when you send them.
reply.mogger: A gilt one, pretty boy. It comes with your first card in the morning. Prop my cards in it.
reply.truecel: A gilt one. It’ll be the best thing in your room by a distance, and it’s two inches tall. It comes with your first card.

no.label: Tell her not to send it

reply.normie: Not one of mine. Fine. Squint at my cards, then. It’ll show in your typing.
reply.mogger: Not one of mine, pretty boy. Suit yourself.
reply.truecel: I’ve seen your room. Fine. Prop them against a pizza box.

arrived.normie: My little chair is at your door, and your first card with it. Prop my cards in it when you send them.
arrived.mogger: My little chair is at your door, pretty boy. Prop my cards in it when you send them.
arrived.truecel: My little chair is at your door. Don’t spill anything on it.

deaths: Her card leaned on the bulb. The curtains went next.
The message sent itself while the smoke alarm screamed.
Alice had the little chair regilded. Nobody asked about you.

yes.label: Tell her you’re into it
player: I’m into it. Tell me more.
That doesn’t scare me. I like it.
Okay. I want to be the one who gives you that.

no.label: Tell her it’s too much
player: That’s a bit much for me.
I don’t think I’m the man for that.
I’d rather keep it simple, honestly.

mogger: I knew you would be. Next time I send you something, you know what to say.
Good. I hoped it would be you. Don’t waste it.
normie: Okay. Nobody’s said that and meant it before. Next time, then.
You mean it? Then next time, show me.
truecel: Really? You? Huh. Next time, then. Don’t get it wrong.
We’ll see. Next time, prove it.

mogger: Shame. Forget I said anything.
Fine. It was a test anyway.
normie: Right. Forget I said it. I shouldn’t have.
Okay. That’s fair. I feel a bit stupid now.
truecel: Of course it’s too much for you. Forget it.
Figures. I don’t know why I told you.

win: That. Exactly that. Don’t say anything else, just stay there.
Nobody has ever done that right. You did it right.
I’m shaking. In a good way. Give me a minute.
Okay. You understand me. That’s terrifying. Do it again soon.
lose: No. That’s not it. That’s not it at all.
You said the words but you didn’t mean them. I can tell.
That just made me feel stupid for telling you.
Wrong. Completely wrong. I’m going to bed.
block: I told you something private and you made it a joke. Goodbye.
I shouldn’t have told you. I won’t make that mistake twice.
Never mind. Don’t message me again.

ask.label: Ask what she’s into
player: So what are you into?
Tell me something you like that you don’t tell people.
What really does it for you?
What are you into, honestly?

dig.label: Ask her to say more
player: Go on. I’m not going anywhere.
Say more. I’m listening.
That’s not the whole answer, is it?
And? Keep going.

leave.label: Leave it there
player: That’s enough for now. Thank you for telling me.
You don’t have to say more. I liked that.

mogger: Hm. Most men push. Noted.
Look at you, being a gentleman about it.
normie: Thank you. Really.
That was nice of you. I’ll remember it.
truecel: Good. I wasn’t going to anyway.
Fine. That’s all you get.

mogger: Not tonight. Keep asking, though. I like that you ask.
You’ll get it out of me. Just not yet.
Ask me again when I’ve had a drink.
normie: I can’t. Not yet. Ask me another time.
Okay, I’ve gone red. Next question.
Maybe when I know you better. I mean that.
truecel: Why would I tell you that?
Nice try. No.
That’s private. You’re not.

push.label: Push her
player: Come on. Tell me.
You can tell me. I won’t laugh.
I want to know. Please.

mogger: Easy. You were doing so well.
Pushing’s not the way in with me. Remember that.
normie: I said not yet. Can we drop it?
Please don’t push. It makes me want to say less.
truecel: Wow. No. Goodnight.
And that’s why I don’t tell people things.

drop.label: Drop it
player: Okay. Whenever you’re ready.
No pressure. Forget I asked.

mogger: See, that’s why I’ll tell you eventually.
Patient. I like patient.
normie: Thank you for not pushing. That matters.
You’re sweet. Ask me again sometime.
truecel: Fine. Thanks, I guess.
Huh. Okay. That was decent of you.

mogger: I keep thinking about what I told you. You didn’t even blink. I liked that.
Still thinking about what you said when I told you. Next time I send you something, you know what to do.
You know my secret now. That makes you dangerous. I like dangerous.
normie: I can’t stop thinking about what I told you. And that you didn’t run.
Is it weird that I told you that? You said you were into it. Were you really?
I told you something I’ve never told anyone. I keep checking that you’re still here.
truecel: I don’t know why I told you that. You’re still here, though. Weird.
Don’t make it a thing. The thing I told you. Unless you want to.
I told you my secret and you didn’t laugh. Most men would have.

mogger: Last time was exactly right. I’ve been useless all day because of it.
You got it right. Nobody gets it right. Do it again soon.
normie: I keep replaying it. You got it exactly right. Thank you, honestly.
I’m still shaking a bit from last time. In the best way.
truecel: Fine. You were good at it. Don’t let it go to your head.
I’ve thought about it more than I want to admit. Again sometime?

MATCH-059.tell: I can only really let go with a man whose story I could print and choose not to. I find the thing in his file, and I sit on it, and that’s the whole thrill.
MATCH-059.label: Give her a secret she could print
MATCH-059.give: Here’s something about me you could print. Don’t.
MATCH-059.hint: Power, mostly. Not the kind people shout about. The quiet kind, where you know something and you don’t use it.
MATCH-059.closer: I read files for a living. Everybody has one thing in theirs they’d die to keep out of the paper. I like knowing it. I like it more when I don’t print it.

MATCH-163.tell: I can only let go to a voice on tape. Not a man in the room. A recording, someone lonely, saying what he really means when he thinks nobody’s listening.
MATCH-163.label: Leave her a voice to keep
MATCH-163.give: I’ll leave you a message tonight. Keep it. Play it when you want.
MATCH-163.hint: Voices. I can fall for a voice before I know whose it is.
MATCH-163.closer: I listen to old tapes at work. People who never thought anyone would hear them. When someone says what they really mean like that, it does something to me.

MATCH-167.tell: I have perfect pitch, and there’s one note. When it’s sounding in the room I come undone. I’ve chased it for years. I think I’ve finally found it.
MATCH-167.label: Hum her the note
MATCH-167.give: Tell me the note. I’ll hum it until you can’t think.
MATCH-167.hint: Sound. There’s one note that undoes me. I’ve chased it for years. I might tell you about it if you ask nicely.

MATCH-169.tell: There’s a cave above the ridge road nobody marks on a map. It’s the only place I can let go. Dry, at dusk, the whole valley going blue.
MATCH-169.label: Tell her you’d meet her there
MATCH-169.give: Draw me the way to the cave. Dusk. I’ll be there.
MATCH-169.hint: Places nobody marks on a map. Somewhere dry and high and quiet, at the exact minute the light goes.

MATCH-172.tell: I need the marks of a real fight fresh on me. A bout at the gym, a ride that hurt. Something my body paid for. Then I’m anyone’s.
MATCH-172.label: Tell her to come straight from the ring
MATCH-172.give: Come straight from the ring. Don’t shower. Bring the bruises.
MATCH-172.hint: Feeling it the next day. A bruise I earned. I don’t trust a body that hasn’t paid for anything.
MATCH-172.closer: I box at a gym by the rail yard. After a real bout, when everything aches, I’m a different person. A softer one. For about an hour.

MATCH-003.tell: I need to see it in your face. The moment you understand what I am, and you’re afraid, and you stay. The staying is everything.
MATCH-003.label: Tell her you’re afraid and staying
MATCH-003.give: I’m afraid of you. I’m staying.
MATCH-003.hint: Honesty. The kind people only show by accident.
MATCH-003.closer: I like the look on a man’s face when he realizes I’m not what he thought. Most of them leave. That’s fine. That’s information.
MATCH-003.closest: There’s a moment when someone sees exactly what I am and goes pale. If he stays after that, I’m his. Nobody has stayed yet.

MATCH-061.tell: Only in the silence after the last record. A night has to have happened, a room has to have emptied, and the needle has to be lifting off the end.
MATCH-061.label: Wait with her for the last record
MATCH-061.give: Play the last record. I’ll wait for the silence with you.
MATCH-061.hint: Endings. The quiet after a night’s over and everyone’s gone home. That’s my favorite sound.

MATCH-062.tell: I can only let go at the exact moment I decide it’s over. Not after. At. The second I know it’s the last time.
MATCH-062.label: Let her decide it’s the last time
MATCH-062.give: Make it the last time, then. I’ll let you.
MATCH-062.hint: Last times. I like knowing something’s the last time while it’s happening.
MATCH-062.closer: I break things off. Nights, people, songs halfway through. There’s a second where I decide it’s over, and I feel more in that second than in all the rest.

MATCH-191.tell: I keep goal. I can only let go on a night something got past me. A penalty I didn’t save, an evening that went wrong. I need to have lost something first.
MATCH-191.label: Tell her to come to you after a loss
MATCH-191.give: Next time one gets past you, come straight to me.
MATCH-191.hint: Losing. Not on purpose. But when something gets past me, I go somewhere else afterward.
MATCH-191.closer: I keep goal for the league team. When I miss one I should have saved, I can’t sleep, I can’t eat, and I want someone. Only then. Isn’t that awful?

MATCH-195.tell: The old vestry, light on, and the hum in the walls. Like a note being held. I lie down and let it go through me and I need a hand on me while it does.
MATCH-195.label: Tell her you’ll be the hand
MATCH-195.give: Lie down in the hum. I’ll be the hand.
MATCH-195.hint: Vibration. There’s a hum in the walls of the old vestry, like a note held forever. I lie on the floor and let it go through me. It’s better with company.

MATCH-206.tell: Kiln nights. The garden dark, the fire through the spyhole going from red to white. That’s the only time. That heat, and someone very still beside me.
MATCH-206.label: Sit very still beside her
MATCH-206.give: Kiln night. I’ll sit beside you and not move until it’s white.
MATCH-206.hint: Heat. Kiln nights, the fire going white through the spyhole. And someone who knows how to sit very still.

MATCH-013.tell: I need to be measured. Properly. Every length taken with a tape and said out loud and written in a book, the way I measure men for their jackets.
MATCH-013.label: Offer to measure her
MATCH-013.give: I’ll get a tape. Every length, out loud, written down.
MATCH-013.hint: Being looked at properly. I measure men for jackets all day. Nobody’s ever measured me. Not like that.

MATCH-029.tell: I need to be dropped. Lifted and let go onto something soft, like the chute throws a rider. That half second of nothing. Then I get back on.
MATCH-029.label: Tell her you’ll catch her, nearly
MATCH-029.give: I’ll lift you and let go. Soft landing. Then you get back on.
MATCH-029.hint: Falling. That half second where nothing’s holding you. I miss it on my days off from the arena.

MATCH-032.tell: Nowhere with a record. No phone, nothing written down, nobody knowing where I am. The desert, the bike, the town’s lights gone. Then I can breathe.
MATCH-032.label: Tell her you’ll leave your phone behind
MATCH-032.give: No phones. No notes. Nobody knows. Just say where.
MATCH-032.hint: Disappearing. No phone, nobody knowing where I am, just the bike and the desert. Want to disappear with me?

MATCH-038.tell: I need to be sewn into something I can’t get out of alone. Tacked shut up the back with real thread. Inside it, the way my customers are inside my dresses.
MATCH-038.label: Tell her you’ll hold the needle
MATCH-038.give: I’ll hold the thread. You tell me where.
MATCH-038.hint: Being held still. I make dresses that hold women in. I think about that more than I should.
MATCH-038.closer: There’s a back seam I tack shut on brides with real thread, so they can’t get out alone. I’ve always wondered what that feels like from the inside.

MATCH-040.tell: I can only let go while someone whispers me a real secret. Theirs. Not a story.
MATCH-040.label: Whisper her a real secret
MATCH-040.give: Come closer. This one’s real. Nobody else knows.
MATCH-040.hint: Secrets. Real ones, whispered. I go to pieces when someone trusts me with something true.

MATCH-049.tell: I can only let go as somebody else. My own name in my own bed does nothing. Call me something else and I’m gone.
MATCH-049.label: Call her by another name
MATCH-049.give: Tonight you’re Lena. I won’t say your real name once.
MATCH-049.hint: Being someone else. My own name gets so tired by the end of a shift.
MATCH-049.closer: I don’t like being me in bed. Maria’s the officer. Maria writes tickets. I’d like to be anyone else for a night. You could choose who.

MATCH-050.tell: Only on a night with no moon. I didn’t choose it. I plotted my own life like a map and the pattern was perfect. I’ve tested it for years.
MATCH-050.label: Wait for the dark of the moon with her
MATCH-050.give: Tell me when the moon’s gone. I’ll keep that night for you.
MATCH-050.hint: Dark nights. I plotted my own life like a map once and found a pattern. It has to do with the moon. Don’t laugh.

MATCH-109.tell: The old junction. In a car, stopped, engine off, the weigh station dark across the yard. My father pulled wrecks out of there. It’s the only place I can let go.
MATCH-109.label: Tell her you’ll sit in the car with her
MATCH-109.give: Engine off at the junction. I’ll sit with you as long as it takes.
MATCH-109.hint: Stillness. A car with the engine off, somewhere my dad used to pull wrecks out of. That’s a strange answer. It’s mine.

MATCH-052.tell: I can only let go with someone who has said yes to doing something for me they shouldn’t. That night. The yes is what does it.
MATCH-052.label: Say yes to something you shouldn’t
MATCH-052.hint: Loyalty. The kind that costs something.
MATCH-052.closer: I like it when someone breaks a rule for me. A small one first. Then I want to know how big a one they’d break.
MATCH-052.closest: There has to be a yes. To something you shouldn’t do, for me, that same night. The yes is what matters. The rest is just the night.

MATCH-053.tell: His rooms. Someone else’s office, his chair, lights off, at the exact hour his diary says he’s somewhere else. I keep the diary, so I always know.
MATCH-053.label: Tell her you’ll meet her in his rooms
MATCH-053.give: Tell me the hour his diary says he’s out. I’ll be in his chair.
MATCH-053.hint: Other people’s rooms. I keep a man’s diary at work. I always know exactly where he is.
MATCH-053.closer: There’s a certain hour when his office is empty and I know it’s empty. I think about that chair more than I think about him.

MATCH-001.tell: I can only let go wearing another woman’s name. A badge from the club’s drawer, a lanyard. I have eleven in a shoebox. You pick.
MATCH-001.label: Pick her a name badge
MATCH-001.give: The one at the bottom of the box. That’s who you are tonight.
MATCH-001.hint: Name badges. Don’t ask. Okay, ask.
MATCH-001.closer: The club keeps a drawer of other women’s name badges. I’ve taken eleven. Wearing somebody else’s name makes me braver.

MATCH-006.tell: I’ve never let anyone tell me what to do. I want you to. Tell me where and how many, and I’ll do it to myself and count them out loud.
MATCH-006.label: Tell her how many, and where
MATCH-006.give: Three. On your thigh. Count them out loud for me.
MATCH-006.closer: I’ve never once let anyone tell me what to do. Not my father, not a coach. Sometimes I wonder what it would feel like to just obey.
MATCH-006.closest: I want someone on the phone giving me orders. Where. How many. And me counting them out loud. I can’t believe I just typed that.

MATCH-042.tell: I arrange other people. Who sits beside whom, who goes home with whom. I watch it begin and that’s my whole night. I’ve never let anyone arrange me.
MATCH-042.label: Offer to arrange her
MATCH-042.give: Let me seat you for once. Right beside me. Watch it begin.
MATCH-042.hint: Seating plans. I’m serious. Who goes home with whom is my whole hobby.
MATCH-042.closer: I arrange people. Dinners, parties, nights. I watch it begin and that’s my evening. Nobody’s ever arranged me. I’ve never let them.

MATCH-043.tell: I pay men to say no. That’s the only way I can let go. I undress, I ask, and I get turned down. Don’t you dare say yes.
MATCH-043.label: Turn her down, slowly
MATCH-043.hint: Restraint. Other people’s. It’s rarer than diamonds, and I can afford diamonds.
MATCH-043.closer: Every man I’ve ever met says yes to me. It’s so dull. I’ve started paying them to do the opposite.
MATCH-043.closest: I ask, I undress, and I get turned down. That’s the only thing that works for me. And you are not allowed to say yes.

MATCH-046.tell: I built the perfect woman and I can only let go once she’s ruined. Lipstick across my cheek, the hair pulled out of its plait. Undo me first.
MATCH-046.label: Tell her you’ll undo her
MATCH-046.give: I’ll ruin the lipstick first. Then the plait. Then you.
MATCH-046.hint: Mess. I spend an hour on my face. I like it best when it’s wrecked.
MATCH-046.closer: I built the perfect woman. Every pin, every line. What I want is somebody to undo her. Lipstick everywhere. Hair down. Ruined.

MATCH-077.tell: I can only let go while I’m telling someone the worst thing I’ve ever seen. Into his ear. All of it. The telling is the release.
MATCH-077.label: Let her tell you everything
MATCH-077.give: Tell me the worst of it. Into my ear. I won’t flinch.
MATCH-077.hint: Talking. Into someone’s ear. The worse the story, the closer I get.
MATCH-077.closer: I’ve seen things at the hospital nobody should. When I tell them, really tell them, all of it, something lets go in me. I need a man who’ll listen to the worst.

MATCH-078.tell: I bet myself at cards. Twice now. I lost both times, and the losing is the thing. The cards going down and the room looking at me as the prize.
MATCH-078.label: Stake her at cards and win
MATCH-078.give: Put yourself on the table. I’m playing to win.
MATCH-078.hint: Cards. High stakes. Higher than money.
MATCH-078.closer: There’s a back room game the Bluebirds’ sons play. I’ve sat in. I’ve put up things I shouldn’t have.
MATCH-078.closest: I’ve put myself up. Twice. I lost both times, and the losing was the thing. I can’t stop thinking about the third.

MATCH-079.tell: I need to be posed and not move. Placed against the glass, told not to speak. If I move, it stops and I’m left there. That’s the part I want most.
MATCH-079.label: Pose her and tell her not to move
MATCH-079.give: Against the glass. Don’t speak. Don’t move. I’ll know.
MATCH-079.hint: Stillness. Being told not to move.
MATCH-079.closer: I model for a painter sometimes. Placed against the window, told not to speak. If I move, he stops. That’s the part I think about after.

MATCH-085.tell: The darkroom. Prints coming up in the tray, faces appearing out of nothing, red light. It’s the only place I can let go.
MATCH-085.label: Tell her you’ll stand in the red light
MATCH-085.give: Red light, the tray, the prints coming up. I’ll be right behind you.
MATCH-085.hint: Red light. Faces coming up out of nothing in the tray. My darkroom is the only place I really relax. Mostly.

MATCH-089.tell: I can only let go on a day I’ve ended someone. A name off a list, a man told he’s finished. I go to bed with it still on me.
MATCH-089.label: Ask who she ended today
MATCH-089.give: Who did you end today? Tell me while it’s still on you.
MATCH-089.hint: Power. Real power. I won’t pretend otherwise.
MATCH-089.closer: Some days I take a name off a list. A man told he’s finished. I go home those nights feeling enormous.
MATCH-089.closest: It only works on a day I’ve finished someone. I go to bed with it still on me. You’re allowed to be afraid of that.

MATCH-203.tell: I can’t let go unless you’ve signed something first. A napkin, a receipt. Your name, in your own hand, handed to me. I keep every one.
MATCH-203.label: Sign something for her
MATCH-203.give: Give me a pen. I’ll sign whatever you put in front of me.
MATCH-203.hint: Signatures. Your name, in your own hand. I keep every one I’m given. Want to give me yours?

postcard.title: The Postcard

hook.mogger: Darling, I have one rule, and I break it for nobody. Before a man has me properly, he writes me a postcard. From a town he has never been to, a town I choose, dated a day I choose, signed with love. Three men have written me one. I married all three. Will you write me the fourth?
hook.normie: A confession, sweet thing. I have one rule. Before a man has me, properly, he writes me a postcard from a town I choose, a town he has never seen, signed with love. Three men have done it. I married all three. Would you write me one?
hook.truecel: Don’t flatter yourself. I have a rule: before any man has me, he writes me a postcard from a town I choose, signed with love. Three men have. I married them. You won’t get that far, but I’m curious what you’d write. Will you?

yes.label: Tell her you’ll write it
yes.player: Send me the card. I’ll write it.

reply.mogger: Oh, good. It comes through your door tomorrow. Write it in bed, darling. That’s the rule.
reply.normie: Tomorrow, through your door. Write it in bed. Sign it properly.
reply.truecel: Fine. It’ll come through your door tomorrow. Don’t make a mess of it.

no.label: Tell her it’s too strange
no.player: A postcard from a town I’ve never been to? That’s too strange for me.

reply.mogger: Strange is the only interesting thing left, darling. Never mind.
reply.normie: Oh. Well. The widower from the casino didn’t think so.
reply.truecel: I didn’t expect much. You’ve met expectations.

card.label: A blank postcard
card.text: A blank postcard of a lake town called {town}, the kind of place with one hotel and a pier. In the corner, in her round hand, a date she has chosen. Underneath: In bed, please. Signed with love. C.

love.label: Write it in bed, signed with love
love.notice: You wrote it in bed, as instructed, and signed it with love. It went back out under your door.

joke.label: Draw a fish on it
joke.notice: You drew a fish on it and wrote wish you were here, sort of. It went back out under your door.

love.mogger: It came. You wrote it in bed, I can tell from the slope of the letters. Nobody has made me wait this well in years. It’s in the album now, darling, next to the engineer’s.
love.normie: It came. You signed it with love. I read it four times and put it in the album, on the page after the engineer’s. You don’t know what that means. That’s all right.
love.truecel: It came. Sweet. I’ve put it in the album under the funny ones. Don’t look so hurt, it’s a compliment, sort of.

postcard.album: My albums. Every card in them was signed with love.
postcard.clue: Every man who wrote Celeste Van Doren a postcard married her and is buried at the Cemetery Chapel with a ribbon on his stone.

after.mogger: The committee has heard your name, darling. I said it to them myself. Sleep well.
after.normie: I said your name at the club today. Just once. People listened.

joke.mogger: A fish. You drew me a fish. I haven’t laughed like that since the rancher fell off his horse. You’re not husband material, darling, and thank heaven.
joke.normie: A fish. Wish you were here, sort of. Well. I suppose that’s honest. The widower from the casino wrote a sonnet.
joke.truecel: A fish. Of course. Don’t write to me again.

late.mogger: No card, darling? The widower from the casino wrote his within the hour. I’ll forgive you. I won’t forget.
late.normie: The card never came back. That’s an answer too.
late.truecel: You couldn’t even manage a postcard. Noted.

deaths: A bottle of very old wine came through the door with a blue ribbon on it. You drank to the fourth husband.
The postcard came back, stamped, from a town you have never been to.
There was a ribbon on your door handle. You never heard the knock.

letter.title: The Letter

hook.mogger: This is mortifying, so I’ll just say it. I can only let go when I’m following instructions. Written ones. What to wear, what hour, what to say at the door. I follow them exactly and then I can stop thinking. Would you write mine?
hook.normie: I’ve never asked anyone this. I can only really let go when I’m following written instructions. The outfit, the hour, the phrase to say at the door. Every word, exactly. Would you write me some?
hook.truecel: I don’t know why I’m asking you. I need written instructions to let go. Exact ones. What to wear, when, what to say. Most men write something stupid. Would you?

reply.mogger: Thank you. Choose carefully. I’ll do every word.
reply.normie: Okay. Choose carefully. I’ll follow every word.
reply.truecel: Fine. Don’t make it stupid.

no.label: Tell her you’re not the type
no.player: I’m not the type to give orders.

reply.mogger: No. Of course. Forget I asked.
reply.normie: That’s all right. I’m a little relieved, honestly.
reply.truecel: No. You wouldn’t be.

label.twinset: Write: the twinset, pearls, and a curtsy
label.window: Write: red lipstick, the window, lamp on
label.phrase: Write: say thank you, sir, and nothing else

player.twinset: The cream twinset. Your pearls. Curtsy when you answer the phone.
player.window: Red lipstick. Stand at your window with the lamp on behind you. Don’t wave.
player.phrase: When you ring me, say thank you, sir. Nothing else. Not one word more.

pick.reply: Written down. Every word. I’ll ring you tomorrow night when it’s done.

twinset.mogger: It’s me. Cream twinset, pearls. I curtsied when I picked up the phone, even though you can’t see me. I did every word.
twinset.normie: It’s me. I’m wearing the twinset. The pearls. I curtsied. I know you couldn’t see. I did it anyway, every word.
twinset.truecel: It’s me. Twinset, pearls, curtsy. I did it. Every word. I feel ridiculous. Don’t laugh.

window.mogger: It’s me. Red lipstick. I’m at the window with the lamp on behind me, not waving. A car slowed down outside. I didn’t move.
window.normie: It’s me. Red lipstick, window, lamp on. I didn’t wave. Someone walked past and looked up. I stayed exactly where you put me.
window.truecel: It’s me. Lipstick, window, lamp. I’ve been standing here an hour. I did it. Every word.

choices.well: Tell her she did it perfectly
choices.wrong: Tell her she got one thing wrong

well.mogger: Perfectly. Say it again. No, don’t, I’ll cry. I’m going to sleep in the pearls.
well.normie: Perfectly. Oh. I don’t think anyone has ever said that to me about anything. Thank you.
well.truecel: Perfectly? Really? Okay. Okay. Thank you. I didn’t expect that from you.

wrong.mogger: One thing. Tell me. No, don’t tell me. Write it down. I’ll do it again tomorrow, right, and every day after.
wrong.normie: One thing? Which? Oh, I hate that. I love that. Write it down and I’ll do it again.
wrong.truecel: One thing wrong. Of course. I did everything you said and it still wasn’t enough. Goodnight.

call.hang: You hung up while I was still standing here in it. Thank you for that, I suppose.

forged.mogger: Your second letter came this morning. Same hand. It said to wear the gray coat and stand at the lodge gate after dark and not to ask why. I did everything it said. Nobody came. Why did you want me there?
forged.normie: Your second letter came this morning. Your hand, I’m sure of it. It said to stand at the lodge gate after dark in the gray coat and not to ask why. I went. Nobody came. Why?
forged.truecel: Your second letter came. Same hand. The lodge gate, after dark, the gray coat. I went. I stood there an hour. Nobody came. Was that a joke?

gatePicture.mogger: I took this at the gate so you could see me waiting. Nobody came.
gatePicture.normie: I took this at the gate. An hour in the gray coat. Nobody came.
gatePicture.truecel: Proof I went. An hour at the gate, in the gray coat. Nobody came.

never.label: Tell her you never wrote it
never.player: I never wrote a second letter, Ruth.
never.reply: Then someone has your hand. Someone very good. I stood at that gate for an hour. I’m frightened now. Thank you for telling me.

claim.label: Tell her you wanted to see if she’d do it
claim.player: I wanted to see if you’d do it.

reply.mogger: You’re a terrible man. I loved every minute at that gate.
reply.normie: That’s cruel. I liked it. I don’t know what that says about me.
reply.truecel: That’s sick. Don’t write to me again.

delphine.never: Don’t be cross, darling. I only borrowed your hand for one letter. It’s a lovely hand. Generous loops.
delphine.claim: You took credit for my letter. Fine. Then you owe me one, and I always collect.

letter.clue: Someone forged your handwriting to send Ruth Calder to the lodge gate after dark; Delphine Moreau can copy anyone’s hand after an hour with a sample.

picture.mogger: So you can see what you made me do.
picture.normie: So you can see I really did it.

letter.missedVm: It’s me. I did every word, exactly, and you didn’t pick up. I’ll try you again tomorrow.

count.title: Match Point

hook.mogger: I need to tell you something and you’re not allowed to be smug about it. I’ve never let anyone tell me what to do. Not my father, not a coach, nobody. I want you to. Ring me, tell me where and how many, and I’ll do it to myself and count them out loud. My safeword is match point. Will you?
hook.normie: Okay. This is hard to say. I’ve never once let anyone give me orders. I want you to. On the phone. You tell me where and how many, and I do it to myself, and count. If it’s too much I say match point and we stop. Would you?
hook.truecel: Don’t make this weird. I’ve never let anyone tell me what to do, and I want to try it with someone who won’t matter. You tell me where and how many, on the phone, I do it and count. Match point means stop. Can you manage that?

yes.label: Tell her you’ll call the count
yes.player: I’ll ring you. I’ll tell you where and how many.

reply.mogger: Tomorrow night, then. I’ll ring you. Be in charge. It suits you.
reply.normie: Tomorrow night. I’ll ring. Match point if it’s too much. I trust you.
reply.truecel: Tomorrow night. I’ll ring. Don’t be pathetic about it.

no.label: Tell her it isn’t for you
no.player: Telling you to hurt yourself isn’t for me.

reply.mogger: Fair. Most men want to be told. You’re a surprise either way.
reply.normie: That’s okay. Honestly, that’s a kind answer.
reply.truecel: Of course it isn’t. Forget it.

open.mogger: It’s me. I lost a set today for the first time in a year. I’m on the bed in my tennis skirt and I’m furious. Tell me.
open.normie: It’s me. I lost a set today. First time in forever. I’m angry and I want to be told. Go on.
open.truecel: It’s me. I lost a set today. Don’t gloat. Just tell me.

open.mogger: It’s me. Training went on for hours and I can barely lift my arm. I’m on the bed. Be careful with me tonight. Tell me.
open.normie: It’s me. I’m sore from training, every muscle. Go easy. Tell me.
open.truecel: It’s me. Everything hurts from training. Don’t overdo it. Tell me.

choices.gentle: Tell her: three, slowly, on her thigh
choices.firm: Tell her: ten, hard, and count every one
choices.stop: Tell her to just lie there and breathe

right.mogger: One. Two. Three. Oh. That was exactly right. How did you know?
right.normie: That was exactly what I needed. I counted every one. I’m shaking a little. In a good way.
right.truecel: Okay. That was right. I hate that you knew.

count.wrong: Match point. Match point. We’re stopping. You weren’t listening to me.

stop.mogger: Just breathe? Fine. That’s the first order I’ve ever liked. I’m breathing.
stop.normie: Okay. I’m lying here breathing. That was kind. I didn’t know I needed that.
stop.truecel: Breathe. Wow. Brave choice. Okay. I’m breathing.

count.hang: You hung up on me mid count. That’s one way to win, I suppose.

picture.mogger: Two nights. I’ve never been told what to do and liked it before. This is for you.
picture.normie: Two nights of you telling me. I’ve never felt so looked after. This is for you.
picture.truecel: Fine. You were good at it. This is for you. Don’t frame it.

count.missedVm: I rang. You didn’t answer. I sat there in my skirt waiting to be told and nobody told me. Don’t do that again.

refusal.title: Refused

hook.mogger: I’ll be honest, because you look like a man who can take it. I pay men to turn me down. I undress, I ask, and they say no. That’s the only thing that does it for me. I’d pay you more than any of them. Would you be the man who says no?
hook.normie: This is going to sound insane. I pay men to say no to me. I ask, and they turn me down, and that’s the only way I can let go. I’d like it to be you. I’ll make it worth your while. Will you?
hook.truecel: Don’t get excited. I pay men to turn me down. I ask, they say no, I go home happy. You look like you’d be very good at saying no to a woman like me. Prove it?

yes.label: Tell her you’ll say no
yes.player: Ask me anything you like. I’ll say no.

reply.mogger: Good. I’ll ask tomorrow. Every no gets a present. They get bigger.
reply.normie: Tomorrow, then. Every time you say no, something comes through your door.
reply.truecel: We’ll see. Tomorrow. Every no gets you something. Try not to cave.

no.label: Tell her you’d rather just say yes
no.player: I’d rather just say yes, to be honest.

reply.mogger: Everybody would. That’s the problem. Never mind.
reply.normie: Oh. That’s sweet. That’s also no use to me at all.
reply.truecel: Of course you would. Goodbye.

asks.mogger: I’m in the suite at the casino hotel with my shoes off. Come up. Please.
asks.normie: I’m at the casino hotel. The suite. Come up tonight. Please.
asks.truecel: Suite at the casino hotel. Shoes off. Come up. I’m asking nicely.

asks.mogger: I’ve sent everyone home. It’s just me, the bath running and the door on the latch. Come up.
asks.normie: The bath’s running and the door’s on the latch. I’m asking again. Come up.
asks.truecel: Bath running. Door on the latch. Second time I’m asking. Come up.

asks.mogger: Last time. I’m begging, which I don’t do. Come up. Please. Say yes.
asks.normie: I’m begging now. Please. Say yes. Come up.
asks.truecel: Last time. I’m begging. Say yes.

afterNo.mogger: God. Thank you. Something’s on its way to you for that.
afterNo.normie: Thank you. Something’s on its way to you.
afterNo.truecel: Good. Hold on to that. Something’s coming through your door for it.

gifts.label: A bottle of champagne
gifts.text: A bottle of very good champagne with a gift tag in a firm hand: For the first no. C.

gifts.label: A silver watch
gifts.text: A heavy silver watch in a box lined with blue silk. The tag: For the second no. Don’t wear it to the club. C.

gifts.label: A casino hotel key card
gifts.text: A key card for the casino hotel’s top suite, in a little envelope. The tag: For the third no. You’ll never use it. That’s the point. C.

gaveIn.mogger: Oh. Oh, no. You said yes. Everybody says yes in the end. I thought you were different.
gaveIn.normie: You said yes. It’s over, then. I’m sorry. It was lovely while you said no.
gaveIn.truecel: Yes. Of course. They all do. Don’t message me again.

won.mogger: Three nos. Nobody has ever lasted three. I’m keeping you, and you’re keeping the watch.
